articles.title: Georgia Restaurant Association Names Wayne Saxe and Howard Aaron Recipients of 2026 GRACE Awards Lifetime Achievement Award
articles.titleKo: Georgia Restaurant Association Names Wayne Saxe and Howard Aaron Recipients of 2026 GRACE Awards Lifetime Achievement Award
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Georgia Restaurant Association (GRA) is proud to announce Wayne Saxe and Howard Aaron of Goldbergs Group as the recipients of the 2026 GRACE Awards Lifetime Achievement Award. The two longtime business partners will be recognized at the Georgia Restaurant Association Crystal of Excellence (GRACE) Awards Gala on Monday, December 7, 2026, for their outstanding careers and lasting contributions to Georgia’s restaurant and hospitality industry. For more than three decades, Saxe and Aaron have shaped Atlanta’s restaurant community, transforming a small neighborhood bagel shop into a thriving, diversified company with operations spanning restaurants, food manufacturing, and aviation food service. Under their leadership, Goldbergs has expanded well beyond its restaurant operations into catering, food manufacturing, and aviation food service, all while maintaining the quality, consistency, and customer service that built its reputation. Their success reflects not only their ability to recognize new business opportunities, but also their commitment to creating jobs, providing long-term career opportunities, and building a company that has become a familiar part of Atlanta families’ lives. Their story began in Johannesburg, South Africa, where both men entered the restaurant industry through different paths. Saxe was working as an accountant when an opportunity to invest in a struggling restaurant led him to discover his passion for the business. Aaron began working in restaurants in 1972, learning the industry from the ground up before eventually opening his own establishment. Their paths crossed when Aaron became a meat supplier for Saxe’s restaurant, and what began as a professional relationship developed into a lasting friendship, family connection, and business partnership. Sharing similar values and a desire to build something of their own, they eventually decided to relocate to the United States and pursue new opportunities. In 1992, Saxe and Aaron acquired Goldberg & Son, a small Atlanta bagel business that would become the foundation of their future success. Through years of hard work, careful expansion, and a commitment to serving quality food, they established Goldbergs Fine Foods as a respected name in Atlanta’s restaurant community. As the company grew, they kept looking for ways to improve operations, expand their offerings, and reach new customers without losing the neighborhood atmosphere and personal service that made Goldbergs successful. Today, the restaurants remain a gathering place for generations of Atlanta families, many of whom have been customers for decades. Saxe’s entrepreneurial vision has driven the company’s expansion beyond traditional restaurant operations. Recognizing the importance of controlling product quality and consistency, he began producing food in-house from a small kitchen at Goldbergs’ West Paces Ferry location. What started with deli favorites such as tuna salad, chicken salad, and other products eventually grew into the company’s broader food manufacturing capabilities. This approach created opportunities to serve customers through new business channels, including aviation food service. It helped establish Goldbergs Group as a diversified food and hospitality enterprise serving customers both in restaurants and through broader aviation and food service channels. Equally important to the company’s success has been Aaron’s focus on its employees and customers. Having worked in nearly every aspect of restaurant operations throughout his career, Aaron believes that successful leadership begins with understanding the people who make a business run. He has consistently emphasized listening to employees, staying involved in day-to-day operations, and leading by example. articles.title: Landry’s and TREW Capital to Acquire Fireman Group Restaurants in $22 Million Deal
articles.titleKo: Landry’s and TREW Capital to Acquire Fireman Group Restaurants in $22 Million Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Landry's is expected to own and operate Bond 45, Café Fiorello, and Trattoria Dell'Arte. TREW Capital will take over Paris Bar, Le Jardin, Café Paradiso, Brooklyn Diner, and Brooklyn Delicatessen. Landry’s and TREW Capital Management are preparing to take ownership of several prominent New York City restaurants following a bankruptcy auction that resulted in a $22.2 million deal for The Fireman Group’s restaurant assets. The transaction received approval Thursday, clearing a major hurdle in the sale of restaurants including Bond 45, Café Fiorello, Trattoria Dell’Arte, Brooklyn Diner, and Paris Bar. According to court documents, Landry’s is expected to own and operate Bond 45, Café Fiorello, and Trattoria Dell’Arte. TREW Capital will take over Paris Bar, Le Jardin, Café Paradiso, Brooklyn Diner, and Brooklyn Delicatessen. Landry’s, owned by billionaire Tilman Fertitta, operates hundreds of restaurants across the country, including Morton’s The Steakhouse, Mastro’s Steakhouse, Del Frisco’s, The Palm, and McCormick & Schmick’s. TREW Capital specializes in acquiring and revitalizing distressed hospitality businesses. According to court documents, the firm operates approximately 80 restaurants employing more than 2,000 people. Its investment history includes BurgerFi, Rubio’s Coastal Grill, Bar Louie, Anthony’s Coal Fired Pizza & Wings, and Iron Hill Brewery & Restaurant. The acquisition offers a path forward for The Fireman Group, whose restaurants have been fixtures in New York City’s dining scene for decades. The company filed for bankruptcy protection in August , less than a year after the death of founder Sheldon “Shelly” Fireman. He opened The Hip Bagel in Greenwich Village in 1963 and spent the following decades building a portfolio of restaurants near some of the city’s best-known cultural destinations. Café Fiorello has operated for more than 50 years, Trattoria Dell’Arte for nearly 40, and Brooklyn Diner for roughly three decades. The restaurant group’s financial troubles stretched back several years, beginning with debt tied to construction projects and losses associated with a restaurant fire. The pandemic compounded those challenges as Broadway closures, declining tourism, and reduced Midtown office traffic hurt sales. The company later turned to merchant cash advances to cover operating expenses, creating additional financial pressure as repayments accumulated. The situation deteriorated further when disputes with certain lenders resulted in credit-card processors withholding millions of dollars in restaurant revenue. The company had less than $100,000 in available cash when it filed for bankruptcy. The Fireman Group’s financial troubles created uncertainty surrounding the future of its restaurants and more than 800 employees. Court documents indicate the business was operating at a loss and had enough available liquidity to continue operating only through the end of October. Landry’s initially submitted an offer of $9.5 million. Its original proposal focused on acquiring Café Fiorello, Trattoria Dell’Arte, and Bond 45 before expanding to additional restaurant assets. The competing bid came from FHGRF LLC, a lender to the bankrupt company. Court documents indicate that Fireman Group CEO Benjamin Grossman owned a 35.8 percent interest in FHGRF, which proposed a transaction that would have allowed him to continue serving as CEO. Following the unsuccessful bid, court documents indicate Grossman is not expected to receive an offer to continue working for the business after the acquisition. Certain other officers and employees have received, or are expected to receive, employment offers from the new owners. articles.title: Outback Steakhouse is Going All In on Better Steaks
articles.titleKo: Outback Steakhouse is Going All In on Better Steaks
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Outback Steakhouse wants to give guests more reasons to return. Outback Steakhouse wants to give customers a new reason to return, and it’s starting with the product that built its reputation nearly four decades ago. The casual-dining chain is reworking nearly every detail of its steak program, such as sourcing, trimming, seasoning, cooking techniques, and employee training. The effort, introduced this month as “Best Steaks Ever,” follows roughly two years of work aimed at improving the quality and consistency of the brand’s signature menu item. Outback announced late last year that it would invest $75 million over the next three years in a turnaround strategy. Of that, $25 million was earmarked for steak excellence and menu redesign. The initiative introduces two new cuts, the Down Under Delmonico Ribeye and New York Strip, alongside familiar dishes such as Victoria’s Barrel-Cut Filet Mignon, the Outback Center-Cut Sirloin, and the Rockhampton Ribeye. Becky Boyd, senior director of food and beverage innovation, says the initiative grew out of a desire to revisit the product responsible for establishing Outback’s identity in casual dining. “We put steaks on the map for casual dining, and we just wanted to raise our own bar,” Boyd says. The work started well before the meat reached restaurant kitchens. Outback collaborated with butchers, farmers, and ranchers to improve sourcing and tighten specifications. Greater attention to trimming helps ensure guests receive the cuts and portions they ordered. Chef Efrem Cutler, Outback’s newly appointed chief steak officer, has worked with the chain for 18 years. He says the improvements came from examining the details of steak preparation, including the cooking equipment and seasonings used to bring out the characteristics of individual cuts. “You can have a great meal. You can have a good meal. Well, we’re spending so much time and attention and focus to sourcing, trimming, tighter specs, ensuring that our guests, if you order a 15-ounce ribeye, it’s a 15-ounce ribeye,” Cutler says. One of the most significant additions is the Delmonico Ribeye, a thick-cut steak with substantial marbling and three distinct muscles that contribute different textures and flavors. Outback developed a new seasoning specifically for the cut and uses an open-flame char grill to create a caramelized exterior. The cooking method offers a contrast to the chain’s traditional seasoned-and-seared preparation on a flat-top grill. Cutler says selecting the appropriate cooking technique is an important part of bringing out the qualities of each steak. “That fire literally licks up on that steak. It caramelizes it. It creates that crust,” Cutler says. The New York Strip provides another option for customers seeking a balance of tenderness, marbling, and beef flavor. Outback also invested in improving its established cuts, particularly the sirloin that helped build the chain’s reputation. Cutler says the goal is to make the quality improvements noticeable across the entire lineup, not just the newest or most expensive selections. Achieving that consistency across a national restaurant system requires changes outside the supply chain. Outback invested in employee training to ensure kitchen teams understand how to select, season, and prepare individual steaks according to customers’ preferences. The company also extended that education to servers, recognizing that a better product doesn’t necessarily translate into a better experience if guests struggle to understand the menu. articles.title: Mexican Concept Puerto Cocina to Open in Dallas’ Design District
articles.titleKo: Mexican Concept Puerto Cocina to Open in Dallas’ Design District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Puerto Cocina, the Mexican, Baja-inspired coastal restaurant in Dallas’ Design District, introduces weekend brunch and a new weekday happy hour. Influenced by the cuisine of Valle de Guadalupe, Baja California, Puerto Cocina’s culinary program celebrates coastal flavors with a focus on fresh seafood, a raw bar featuring crudos and tiraditos, house-made masa crisps and an emphasis on shellfish and caviar. Building on this distinctive approach, the restaurant’s new weekend brunch, available Saturdays and Sundays from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., features Mexican-inspired brunch favorites, fresh seafood and savory dishes, while happy hour, offered Tuesday through Friday from 5–7 p.m. exclusively in the bar lounge, introduces curated pairings of creative cocktails and flavorful bites for just $16 each. Puerto Cocina’s new weekend brunch offers a menu that balances classic brunch favorites with bold, unexpected flavors. Guests can enjoy dishes like Steak & Eggs – grilled bavette, potato hash, over-easy eggs and salsa tatemada; Chilaquiles – choice of chicken, shrimp or filet, topped with Monterey cheese, red or green salsa, pickled red onion, fried egg and crispy nopales; and Banana Bread French Toast – banana brûlée, pastry cream and café de olla syrup. For a lighter option, the Chia Seed Pudding combines strawberry jam, coconut-chia pudding, matcha, toasted coconut and pepitas. In addition to the brunch specialties, guests can enjoy a variety of dishes from Puerto Cocina’s menu during brunch, including fresh seafood, tacos, tortas and salads. Standouts include the Baja Taco with tempura-battered fish, cabbage and serrano confit slaw; Aguachile de Atun – Aguachile negro, pearl onions, jicama and candied jamaica; Milanesa Torta – chicken milanesa, cabbage slaw, serrano confit, jalapeno crema, avocado, chiltepin aioli and cotija; and Burrata Salad – figs, beets, Cara Cara oranges, candied pepitas, charred cebollita dressing and mustard frill. Puerto Cocina is also introducing a new happy hour, available Tuesday through Friday from 5–7 p.m. exclusively in the bar lounge. The menu features Curated Bocado Pairings for $16 each – thoughtfully combining a signature cocktail with a bite for an elevated and unique take on the traditional happy hour experience. Guests can choose from four distinctive pairings: Mussel Aguachile & Spritz: Confit mussels with coconut curry aguachile paired with a spritz featuring damiana, strawberry and sparkling rosé. Crab Cake & Margarita: Crab cake with anchovy aioli and salsa pelirroja paired with a margarita featuring matcha, yuzu and tequila. Butter Braised Scallop & Milk Punch: A butter-braised scallop with mignonette butter, pasilla and smoked trout roe paired with a milk punch featuring guava, mezcal and charred sourdough. Fried Oyster & Negroni: A masa-crusted oyster with pistachio salsa macha paired with a Negroni featuring melon, Salers aperitif and gin. Each pairing is designed to showcase the interplay between Puerto Cocina’s seafood-forward culinary program and creative cocktail offerings, giving guests an opportunity to experience the restaurant’s distinctive flavors in an approachable format. Puerto Cocina’s weekend brunch is available Saturdays and Sundays from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., while happy hour is offered Tuesday through Friday from 5–7 p.m. in the bar lounge only. Walk-ins are welcome, and reservations are available through Resy. The post Mexican Concept Puerto Cocina to Open in Dallas’ Design District appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Home Run Inn Launches Largest TV Campaign in its 103-Year History
articles.titleKo: Home Run Inn Launches Largest TV Campaign in its 103-Year History
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Home Run Inn Pizza, the iconic Chicago pizza brand known for bringing its tavern-style pizza from its restaurants to freezer aisles across the country, is launching a new integrated marketing campaign to drive awareness and demand for its growing CPG offering in key markets nationwide. The campaign is led by a set of new television commercials that tell the unique family owned, tavern-to-table story that makes Home Run Inn Pizza a standout in the frozen pizza category. The spots feature award-winning blues guitarist, singer/songwriter, and legend, “Billy Blues” Fruteland Jackson, further bringing the brand’s Chicago heritage to life. The campaign represents the single largest television investment in Home Run Inn’s 103-year history. The creative will begin airing in select markets nationwide in late October to coincide with National Tavern-Style Pizza Day on October 22. Online and connected video, streaming audio, out-of-home, and display advertising will support the television campaign. Home Run Inn Pizza has been serving its signature tavern-style pizza in Chicago for more than 75 years and today operates six pizzerias throughout Chicagoland. In the late 1950s, the family began par-baking and freezing those same pizzas for customers and local grocery stores, laying the foundation for a frozen pizza business that now reaches consumers nationwide. For Home Run Inn and quench, the new campaign taps into something few frozen pizza brands can claim: a product with a generational restaurant legacy behind it. “We know we have a great product and a story that resonates with consumers. The opportunity now is making sure more people know about it as we expand into new markets,” said Home Run Inn Pizza CEO Dan Costello. “This campaign is about getting our name in front of more people and sharing what makes our pizza special.” “A lot of brands can sell frozen pizza. Home Run Inn delivers a genuine Chicago pizza experience,” said quench CEO Michael Pavone. “That story is real and it’s authentic. It also gives us something powerful to work with creatively. Our job is to turn that authenticity into something that gets attention and drives sales.” The new television work is part of Home Run Inn Pizza’s ongoing efforts to introduce its signature tavern-style pizza to more consumers and build the brand in markets across the country. Additional branding support is expected to roll out in early 2027. The post Home Run Inn Launches Largest TV Campaign in its 103-Year History appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Names John Palumbo VP of Franchise Development
articles.titleKo: Launch Family Entertainment Names John Palumbo VP of Franchise Development
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Launch Family Entertainment (Launch), a premier indoor family entertainment concept, has named John Palumbo Vice President of Franchise Development as the brand strengthens its leadership team and advances its national growth strategy. Palumbo brings nearly two decades of franchise development experience and an early-career foundation in sports and recreation operations. He began his career in athletic administration and operated sports clubs in New York City before transitioning into franchising. Since then, he has held development leadership roles across the restaurant, education, and service industries with established franchise organizations including A&W Restaurants, H&R Block, and Primrose Schools, where he led national development strategies, franchise sales, and multi-unit growth initiatives. Most recently, Palumbo served as Vice President of Franchise Development at Celebree School. In his new role, Palumbo will lead Launch’s franchise development strategy and guide the brand’s expansion into new and existing markets. As Launch looks toward 2027, he will also help identify strategic development opportunities that align with the brand’s evolving model and long-term growth objectives. “As we continue advancing Launch Family Entertainment’s growth strategy, having the right leadership and strong franchisee relationships is critical,” said Craig Erlich, CEO of Launch Family Entertainment. “John has a proven track record of identifying development opportunities and partnering with seasoned multi-unit operators. His perspective will be invaluable as we strengthen our franchise system and bring the Launch Experience to more communities.” Launch has accelerated its development efforts throughout 2026, opening new parks, signing development agreements, and securing new leases nationwide. The brand is also exploring more flexible park formats to accommodate a broader range of real estate opportunities and market needs while maintaining the core Launch Experience. With 30 locations across 15 states and multiple additional parks in development, Launch continues to target strategic markets and partner with qualified franchise operators. “What stood out to me about Launch is the flexibility of the model and the opportunity that creates for thoughtful, strategic growth,” said Palumbo. “There is a real sense of alignment across the leadership team and franchise community around where the brand is headed and the experience we want to provide guests. I look forward to building on that foundation, helping our franchise partners grow, and identifying the right opportunities to bring Launch into new markets.” Launch Family Entertainment offers a scalable, multi-unit franchise opportunity within the evolving family entertainment industry, combining diverse attractions, immersive experiences, and hospitality offerings to engage a broad demographic. The brand continues to seek qualified franchise partners with strong operational capabilities and the financial capacity to support strategic growth across the United States. Prospective franchisees can learn more at https://franchise.launchfamilyentertainment.com/signup. articles.titleKo: Golden Corral Franchisee Eric Holm Named 2026 IFA Franchisee of the Year
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Holm operates 18 Golden Corral buffets throughout Central Florida. Eric Holm, Golden Corral franchise owner and founder of Metro Corral, was recently named a 2026 Franchisee of the Year by the International Franchise Association (IFA). Announced at the IFA26 Advocacy Summit in Washington, D.C., Sept. 14 -16, the award recognizes franchise owners who demonstrate leadership through community involvement, workforce development, and franchise mentorship. Holm operates 18 Golden Corral buffets throughout Central Florida, including several high-performing locations. Beyond the success of his own buffets, he has established himself as a resource for other franchisees in the Golden Corral system by mentoring his fellow operators and serving multiple terms on the brand’s Franchise Advisory Council. Holm’s focus on developing and retaining strong restaurant teams has also contributed to one of the lowest management turnover rates within the Golden Corral system. “Eric exemplifies the kind of franchisee leadership that has strengthened our franchise system for decades,” said David Conklin, Chief Development Officer of Golden Corral. “He has built a strong organization while remaining committed to his community and the values of our brand, and his continued investment in Golden Corral is a meaningful reflection of the strength of our franchise system.” That commitment to service is rooted in Holm’s own experience. Raised by a single mother as one of five children, Holm and his family once relied on the Salvation Army for a Thanksgiving meal. For more than 30 years, he has carried that experience with him, volunteering each Thanksgiving with the Salvation Army to help provide approximately 20,000 meals to people throughout Central Florida. “Franchisees of the Year demonstrate what franchising is all about; individuals who have committed their lives and careers to the betterment of those around them, building something bigger than themselves,” said Matt Haller, President and CEO of the International Franchise Association. “Through their leadership, they create jobs and build careers, give back to their communities, and support other franchisees, all while exemplifying the entrepreneurial spirit at the heart of franchising. We are proud to recognize Eric with IFA’s highest honor for individual franchisees and celebrate his commitment to making a difference both within his business and beyond.” For more information about Golden Corral and franchise opportunities, visit goldencorral.com/franchise. Sport entertainment leader, Topgolf has announced a multi-year partnership with John Daly, that will see the two-time Major winner take part in a number of activities at venues around the U.S., bringing his larger-than-life personality and fan-favorite appeal into the Topgolf experience. The partnership builds on Daly’s appearances at Topgolf’s venue in Augusta in 2026 during the first Major of the year, and will expand to include live appearances, branded content, and unique experiences across Topgolf venues. “I love the vibe at Topgolf,” said John Daly. “It’s a place where you can smash a golf ball, listen to music, have a drink and enjoy yourself with friends and family. articles.title: Proper Good Makes It’s London Debut in the Heart of Soho
articles.titleKo: Proper Good Makes It’s London Debut in the Heart of Soho
articles.originalSummary: Proper Good [PG], made its London debut with the opening of a new restaurant in the heart of Soho, bringing its fresh, fast and flavour-packed food and drink concept to the capital. Located at 3 Soho Street, just off Oxford Street, the restaurant is the brand’s first site in England and a major step in its continued expansion. Londoners can get stuck into the PG bold and flavour-packed menu, where classic favourites get a fresh and nutritional twist. Expect everything from South Korean-inspired UFO buns and loaded salads to rice bowls packed with flavours including Miso Tuna, Gochujang Tofu and Chimi Chicken. On the side, there’s Feta Tzatziki, Ginger Slaw and more, plus PG signature drinks, electrolyte blends and its social media-famous frozen fruit desserts topped just the way you like them. Professor Green, Musician, Musician, Foodie and Partner for PG, said: “Opening PG in my home city feels surreal. This is the place that inspired me in so many ways growing up, so bringing the brand to London is a really proud moment. “I can’t wait for people to experience the food for themselves. I believe that the best ideas come from creativity, personality and different influences coming together, and that’s what we’ve built with PG. Being able to bring that back to the city and communities that helped shape me makes this opening even more special.” PG is founded in partnership with Professor Green and Hero Brands, the team behind successful concepts including German Doner Kebab and Sides with the Sidemen. Rebecca Tye, Managing Director of PG, added: “Opening in London is a major milestone for PG and an important step in our growth journey. As one of the world’s most influential food and culture destinations, Soho is the perfect place for us to continue building the brand and introducing more people to what PG stands for. “As the brand continues to evolve, our focus is on creating something that reflects today’s culture, brings people together through shared experiences and delivers what modern consumers value – a community brand that delivers quality in a fun way.” The launch has been supported by local out-of-home media, partnering with Outernet London, and is teasing the launch on their iconic screens outside Tottenham Court Road.

articles.title: NINE: Liverpool and Wales Legend Ian Rush Launches Welsh Single Malt Whisky with Penderyn Distillery
articles.titleKo: NINE: Liverpool and Wales Legend Ian Rush Launches Welsh Single Malt Whisky with Penderyn Distillery
articles.originalSummary: Liverpool and Wales legend Ian Rush MBE , whose extraordinary senior career produced 411 goals in 892 appearances , has joined forces with Penderyn Distillery, the home of Welsh whisky, to launch NINE , a nine-year-old Welsh single malt whisky matured in Tawny port casks and personally selected by Rush himself. Named after the number nine shirt Rush made famous at Anfield, NINE brings together two unmistakably Welsh names while celebrating one of the most prolific goalscoring careers in British football. Across a senior career spanning Chester, Liverpool, Juventus, Leeds United, Newcastle United, Sheffield United, Wrexham and Sydney Olympic, Rush made 892 appearances and scored 411 goals . At Liverpool, he became the greatest goalscorer in the club’s history, scoring 346 goals in 660 appearances across 15 seasons on Merseyside. On 18 October 1992, his 287th Liverpool goal, against Manchester United at Old Trafford, took him beyond Roger Hunt’s previous record. More than three decades later, Rush’s Liverpool record remains unmatched. For Wales, Rush scored 28 goals in 73 international appearances , becoming his country’s record goalscorer in 1993. He held the record for 25 years until Gareth Bale surpassed it in 2018. Now, the number that defined Rush’s career has inspired a whisky created to carry his name . NINE Years. Number NINE. NINE is a nine-year-old Welsh single malt matured in Tawny port casks , with Rush personally involved in selecting the liquid at Penderyn. The nine-year maturation was chosen as a direct reference to the shirt number synonymous with Rush’s career, creating a natural connection between the whisky and one of football’s most famous number nines. But while the whisky’s name draws directly from football, its striking presentation takes its inspiration from somewhere else entirely. NINE is presented in a distinctive bottle with a gold finish, its design inspired by the sophistication, glamour and cinematic style. The pack is designed by threebrand based in Leith, Edinburgh. The gold finish is deliberately not based on the red colours of club and country instead, the bottle has been conceived as a premium standalone object, giving NINE an identity beyond conventional football merchandise and positioning it equally as a collector’s piece, luxury gift and Welsh single malt whisky. The gold aesthetic evokes timeless British style and a sense of occasion, giving NINE a distinctive presence designed to stand out in a whisky collection, behind a bar or on display. The result is a whisky that celebrates Rush’s footballing legacy without simply reproducing the traditional colours associated with his career. “I wore the number nine for Liverpool and it means everything to me, so this had to be nine, nine years old and named after the shirt,” said Ian Rush. “I’m a proud Welshman and Penderyn is Wales’ whisky, so there was never any other distillery I wanted to do this with. I tasted my way through the casks myself and I wasn’t going to put my name on it unless I’d be happy pouring it for my family and friends. “I also wanted the bottle to look completely different. It’s stylish and has a bit of glamour about it. “It’s for Liverpool fans, it’s for Wales, but it’s also for anyone who appreciates a proper single malt. I can’t wait to put a bottle in the hands of a few old teammates and acquaintances.” The Goalscorer’s Goalscorer Rush’s career remains one of the defining goalscoring stories of modern British football. His movement and ability to appear behind defenders earned him the nickname “The Ghost”, while his partnership with Kenny Dalglish became one of the most celebrated attacking combinations in Liverpool history. Among his defining performances was the 1986 FA Cup Final , when Rush scored twice as Liverpool came from behind to defeat Everton 3-1 at Wembley and complete the League and FA Cup Double. articles.title: National Restaurant Association Launches Latest Evolution of Kids LiveWell Program
articles.titleKo: National Restaurant Association Launches Latest Evolution of Kids LiveWell Program
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Finding delicious, balanced meals for children just got a little easier at thousands of restaurants across the country. Today, the National Restaurant Association launched the latest evolution of the award-winning Kids LiveWell program, a new website that helps families find restaurants offering balanced menu options for children that have been dietitian-verified to meet the program’s science-based nutrition criteria. Parents and caregivers can now easily go online and search for a restaurant near them that has committed to offering a selection of menu items for children that focus on real foods like fruits, vegetables, meat or meat alternatives, whole grains, and dairy. What is the Kids LiveWell program? Kids LiveWell is a voluntary restaurant industry program that certifies kids’ menu items against specific criteria. Registered dietitians verify each item based on menu and nutrition information provided by participating restaurants. To participate, restaurants must offer at least two meals and two sides that meet science-based nutrition criteria and include at least two food groups. Dietitians evaluate each item for calories, saturated fat, trans fat, added sugars, sodium and servings of key food groups, including fruits, vegetables, dairy, meat or meat alternatives, and whole grains. Participating restaurants must also maintain default kids’ menu beverage options of water, milk, or 100% fruit or vegetable juice. The long-standing program is the centerpiece of the restaurant industry’s commitment to providing better-for-you choices, especially for children. “Restaurants that offer Kids LiveWell-certified menu options are helping families find meals they can choose with confidence,” said Michelle Korsmo, President & CEO of the National Restaurant Association. “This new website, with an expanded roster of participating brands, makes it easier for parents and caregivers to find restaurant options that meet their family’s needs when dining out.” How does the new Kids LiveWell website work? The new Kids LiveWell website will be a trusted go-to resource for families that illustrates the program’s nutrition requirements and showcases participating brands. Parents can go to the mobile-ready site, kidslivewell.com , and click on the Good Food Finder at the top of the page to see a list of participating restaurants. To explore Kids LiveWell offerings at participating restaurants, simply click the logo to view approved meals. Parents can find an overview of the Kids LiveWell nutrition requirements at the top of the participating restaurants page on kidslivewell.com and can take an in-depth look at the nutrition criteria in the Kids LiveWell white paper here . “The new Kids LiveWell website is another way restaurants are delivering value to the families they serve, including their youngest guests,” said Korsmo. “Dining out remains an important part of daily life and families are paying closer attention to what they order and the value they receive. Paired with this new digital tool, Kids LiveWell menu options help participating operators strengthen their value proposition and meet the needs of today’s consumers.” Which restaurants participate in Kids LiveWell? Kids LiveWell restaurants fit the needs of every family’s lifestyle. Menu options are available across quickservice, fast casual, and fullservice restaurants, including both independent operators and national chains. Regardless of restaurant type, all participants must meet the same rigorous nutrition standards, which are independently verified by third-party dietitians. articles.title: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira Welcomes Newly Appointed Chinese Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau, Presenting Cantonese Cuisine Reimagined Through Craft, Heritage and Memory
articles.titleKo: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira Welcomes Newly Appointed Chinese Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau, Presenting Cantonese Cuisine Reimagined Through Craft, Heritage and Memory
articles.originalSummary: Michelin-recommended contemporary Cantonese restaurant Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira , Tsim Sha Tsui, welcomes Lau Sze-yau as its new Executive Chef. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. These fundamentals underpin a newly unveiled à la carte menu which retains signature classics for convivial celebrations, reimagines family favourites with nostalgic warmth, and introduces inventive creations that heighten the excitement of fine Chinese dining. Uniting Chef Lau’s culinary ingenuity with modern aesthetics in the restaurant’s elegant setting, the menu presents an exquisite feast designed to engage all the senses. With over two decades of culinary experience, Executive Chef Lau Sze-yau’s gastronomic journey was first sparked in childhood during family reunion dinners. Watching elders transform simple, fresh ingredients into a banquet of rich flavours – and seeing the joy it brought to loved ones – deeply moved him. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. Chef Lau’s career in Cantonese gastronomy spans leading hospitality brands including The Hong Kong Bankers Club, Hong Kong Parkview and the Clearwater Bay Golf & Country Club. He honed his expertise at the Chinese Culinary Institute under the Vocational Training Council, completing advanced master classes and the Master Chef Course in Chinese Cuisine, where he was honoured as Outstanding Trainee of the 10th programme. His talent has earned widespread industry recognition, with consecutive gold and silver awards at the Vocational Training Council’s Asian Culinary Exchange from 2017 to 2019. Dedicated to promoting Cantonese culinary culture, he serves on the committees of the Asia Art of Cuisine Society and the Hong Kong Chinese Chefs Association, and was a judge at the 2019 Hong Kong International Culinary Classic. I am thrilled to join Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira and to share my contemporary vision of Cantonese cuisine, conceived through craft, heritage and memory, with multi-generational families of Hong Kong gourmands and guests from around the world,” says Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau. “Grounded in authentic Cantonese flavours, my creations are elevated with modern touches in refined and often surprising presentations, ingredient pairings and culinary techniques. In harmony with the restaurant’s elegant concept, my goal is to curate memorable dining journeys that captivate through taste, aroma and visual beauty. Under the leadership of Chef Lau, Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira unveils nine new signature creations spanning appetisers, main courses and desserts – each testament to his versatility and creativity. This flavour journey unfolds across three chapters: infusing dynamic new life into traditional Cantonese frameworks, honouring time‑tested craftsmanship, and evoking cherished memories at the table. Guests are invited to immerse themselves in the chef’s storybook of tastes, savouring the heritage of Chinese culture while reconnecting with “the joy of memory” – nostalgic moments when flavour, love and happiness intertwined around the family table. Chapter I – Creative Artistry Premium ingredients, handpicked for quality and seasonality, are reimagined through refined techniques, inventive flavour pairings and contemporary presentation. Classic Cantonese dining is elevated into discoveries, where precision and artistry reveal fresh dimensions of taste. articles.title: Texas-Based Hotel Thompson Austin Taps Sergio Ledesma to Lead Rooftop Restaurant
articles.titleKo: Texas-Based Hotel Thompson Austin Taps Sergio Ledesma to Lead Rooftop Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Thompson Austin and tommie Austin are pleased to announce the appointment of Sergio Ledesma as executive chef of Arriba Abajo Rooftop Cantina, the hotels’ signature rooftop restaurant. Located on the fourth floor of Thompson Austin, just steps from the city’s famed Sixth Street, Arriba Abajo pairs sweeping views of the downtown skyline with vibrant Mexican cuisine inspired by the flavors of Oaxaca, Yucatán and Tulum. Originally from Mexico, Ledesma brings a deep appreciation for Mexican culinary traditions, ingredients and hospitality to Arriba Abajo, shaped by a career spanning acclaimed restaurants and hotels. After studying at The Culinary Institute of America, he went on to serve as executive chef at La Central San Pedro, an upscale steakhouse in San Pedro Garza García, Mexico, before making his way to Austin, where he most recently led the culinary program at Hotel Van Zandt, a boutique hotel in the heart of downtown and home to the acclaimed restaurant Geraldine’s. “Having spent the last several years in Austin, I’ve built a deep appreciation for this city and its incredible culinary community,” said Ledesma. “What excites me about Arriba Abajo is the opportunity to bring the flavors and traditions I grew up with in Mexico to our guests and share them in a way that feels genuine and approachable. I’m looking forward to working with the team, continuing to learn and creating a place where people can come together and enjoy great food.” At Arriba Abajo, Ledesma will draw on his Mexican roots and years of culinary expertise to further shape the restaurant’s menu, emphasizing bold flavors, seasonal ingredients and thoughtful technique. Inspired by the family meals and food traditions of his childhood, his approach reflects a belief that great dining goes beyond the plate, bringing people together through food, storytelling and a shared sense of hospitality. Ledesma also brings fresh energy to Arriba Abajo’s hidden mezcalería, También, with a reimagined take on its multisensory, multi-course tasting, Mezcal, También. Available exclusively on November 12 and 19, a new seven-course experience will celebrate Mexico’s culinary diversity, with each course highlighting the cuisine of one of the country’s seven regions. The program will continue with specialty holiday lineups throughout December before transitioning in 2027 to monthly rotating menus, each dedicated to the culinary traditions of a different Mexican region. articles.title: Ted’s Montana Grill to Close Locations on Thanksgiving and Christmas
articles.titleKo: Ted’s Montana Grill to Close Locations on Thanksgiving and Christmas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ted’s Montana Grill, the classic American grill known for elevated, timeless cuisine with bold flavors and fresh, authentic ingredients, has announced that all locations will close annually on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day so the team can celebrate with the people who matter most. “We’re grateful for our passionate, dedicated team, who give their best year-round and bring what we call the ‘Big Sky Spirit’ to life every day,” said George McKerrow, CEO and co-founder of Ted’s Montana Grill. “A spirited culture is built on the belief that the best guest experiences start from a team that feels supported and valued. Thanksgiving has been one of our biggest sales days, but family comes first, and giving our team time with loved ones is one way we show our appreciation.” Ted’s commitment to its team comes during a year of positive momentum. Guest ratings on Yelp and Google have increased for four consecutive years. Internal management survey results also underscore the strength and engagement of Ted’s leadership team, with 100% participation and an impressive score of 3.97 out of 4, reflecting strong confidence in the Ted’s Montana Grill concept. The spirit of the season will extend beyond Ted’s own team too. Ted’s Montana Grill will host special holiday dinners for families facing hardship, offering a welcoming place to gather, share a heartwarming meal, and experience the warmth of genuine hospitality. Community members are invited to nominate families who have faced challenges or demonstrated extraordinary strength, kindness or generosity. Ted’s is also renewing its commitment to an exceptional dining experience. Every single team member will receive refreshed training on delivering the ‘Big Sky Spirit’ at every step of the guest journey. This includes comprehensive steak training, preparing feel-good, high-quality meals in-house with no microwaves or freezers, and treating every guest like family in their own home. “Our people are at the heart of everything we do, and every guest deserves to feel that from the moment they walk through our doors,” said Ted’s Montana Grill President Kristi Martin. “The Big Sky Spirit is about more than great food. It’s about genuine hospitality, attention to every detail, and doing things the right way, with no shortcuts. We’re committed to delivering a best-in-class experience every time, serving real food for real people, and making every guest feel like part of the family.” HELP US SHARE THE SPIRIT OF THE SEASON. articles.title: OneDine Introduces Conversational Tableside Ordering Technology
articles.titleKo: OneDine Introduces Conversational Tableside Ordering Technology
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Restaurant operators have spent decades trying to solve one of the industry’s most persistent problems: every time a server leaves, valuable knowledge leaves with them. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, there are approximately 2.3 million servers working in restaurants today, yet every year more than 423,000 positions must be filled, creating a continuous cycle of onboarding, training, and knowledge loss. Today, OneDine launched Restaurant Ordering Mentor (ROM™), a patent-pending, POS-agnostic server intelligence platform built to address one of the restaurant industry’s largest hidden profit drains: workforce churn. As operators face constant recruiting, onboarding and retraining cycles, ROM puts the intelligence of the restaurant directly into the hands of every server, reducing dependence on menu memorization, accelerating productivity, improving consistency, and freeing teams to focus on hospitality. For operators, that means faster ramp-up and stronger execution. For restaurant executives, it means increasing profitability in an industry where turnover remains a constant challenge. Instead of memorizing where modifiers live, learning menu structures, and searching through screens while standing at the table, ROM allows servers to enter orders with just a few keystrokes, as if they’re texting on a phone. ROM quickly and intuitively interprets even just a couple of letters, mapping to any restaurant’s menu data and guides servers along the ordering flow, ensuring every order is placed accurately, aligned with the brand’s business goals, like required selections, dietary accommodations, and even preferred pairings and upsells. The result is faster onboarding, greater consistency, improved productivity and more time for servers to focus on true hospitality. “The future of restaurant technology isn’t about replacing people. It’s about helping people perform at their best,” commented Mike Axiotis, President and CEO, Lehigh Valley Restaurant Brands and Chair, National Restaurant Association Board of Directors. “For decades, our industry has invested heavily in systems that improve transactions and operations. The next frontier is helping frontline teams deliver better hospitality. That’s why innovations like ROM are so interesting. They represent a shift toward technology that strengthens the human side of restaurants rather than competing with it.” “For more than 30 years, we’ve asked servers to adapt to technology that was never designed for the way they actually work,” said Rom Krupp, Founder and CEO of OneDine. “We train them to memorize menus, learn modifier paths, navigate screens, and master complex systems before they can fully focus on the guest. ROM turns that model on its head. Instead of forcing people to think like the POS, ROM allows technology to work the way people naturally communicate. We believe that’s one of the most significant changes to tableside ordering since the POS was introduced.” After 20 months of intense R&D, field testing and validation, ROM is available immediately for full-service restaurant deployments. Wagamama has spent more than three decades building a recognizable restaurant brand in the U.K. Its Asian-inspired menu, communal seating, and distinctive dining experience have helped the chain grow to more than 170 locations across its home market. The U.S. has been a different story. Despite operating in America for nearly two decades, Wagamama has just five restaurants, including two in New York City and locations in Boston, Arlington, Virginia, and Tampa, Florida. The brand has struggled to translate its overseas popularity into a meaningful U.S. presence. CEO Stephen Judge believes he knows why. The company initially tried to replicate its successful British restaurant model without sufficiently accounting for differences in American dining habits. “When they brought Wagamama to the U.S., they really brought it with a British playbook, a British recipe book and concept and seating layout that had been proven to be very successful in the U.K. And frankly speaking, they didn’t adapt it for the U.S. market,” Judge says. Judge, a Liverpool native whose restaurant career includes experience with Seasons 52 and Bonefish Grill, was brought aboard to help correct that disconnect and establish a foundation for domestic expansion. One of the first moves involved relocating the company’s U.S. corporate office from Midtown Manhattan to Tampa. His first six months also included extensive consumer research to determine which elements of Wagamama resonated with American guests and which needed to change. The company conducted menu satisfaction studies examining everything from portion sizes and pricing to ingredients and perceived value. Focus groups in New York, Boston, and Washington, D.C., provided additional feedback on restaurant layouts, seating arrangements, and menu presentation. Some of the findings challenged longstanding elements of the Wagamama experience. American guests weren’t particularly fond of the brand’s signature communal tables or backless benches, which they considered uncomfortable during longer dining occasions. They preferred traditional chairs and flexible table configurations that could accommodate different party sizes. Wagamama has since incorporated those preferences into its U.S. restaurants, including locations in Tampa and New York. The research also uncovered some surprising demographic characteristics. Women account for 57 percent of Wagamama’s American customers, and more than 30 percent of its guests earn over $150,000 annually. Those findings helped inform a significant overhaul of the brand’s food and beverage offerings. Wagamama recently introduced 26 new dishes and 15 Asian-inspired drinks, representing one of its most substantial efforts to tailor the concept to American consumers. New beverage platforms include Wagaritas and Wagatinis, featuring selections such as Thai chili margaritas, lychee martinis, and ube espresso martinis. articles.title: The True Cost of a Restaurant Renovation: What Owners Often Overlook
articles.titleKo: The True Cost of a Restaurant Renovation: What Owners Often Overlook
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The financing structure used for a renovation can influence the restaurant’s financial flexibility long after construction is completed. For full-service restaurant owners, renovations can be an important investment in the future of their business. Updating an aging dining room, replacing kitchen equipment, or redesigning an inefficient layout may improve the guest experience and support long-term growth. However, a restaurant renovation can also create financial challenges that extend well beyond the construction budget. Unexpected expenses, temporary closures, reduced seating capacity, and financing obligations can place significant pressure on cash flow. Before beginning a major renovation, restaurant owners should carefully evaluate the financial decisions that can determine whether the project strengthens the business or creates unnecessary risk. The Construction Estimate Is Not the Entire Budget Restaurant renovation budgets often begin with contractor estimates, equipment costs, and interior improvements. Yet additional expenses can accumulate throughout the project. Permits, architectural services, inspections, technology upgrades, furniture, installation, and unexpected repairs may substantially increase the total investment. Older restaurant properties may also require electrical, plumbing, ventilation, or accessibility improvements that were not anticipated during the initial planning process. Consider a hypothetical full-service restaurant planning a $400,000 renovation. If the owner allocates the entire amount to construction and equipment, an unexpected 15 percent increase in project costs would create an additional $60,000 expense. Without adequate reserves or available financing, the owner may be forced to delay construction, reduce the project’s scope, or use funds intended for normal operations. A realistic renovation budget should include contingency funds and sufficient liquidity to address unexpected expenses. Lost Revenue Can Be More Expensive Than Expected One of the most frequently overlooked renovation costs is the revenue a restaurant may lose while construction is underway. Some projects require a complete temporary closure. Others allow the restaurant to remain open but reduce seating capacity or disrupt normal service. For full-service restaurants, where revenue depends heavily on dining room availability and customer experience, even temporary disruptions can have meaningful financial consequences. Consider a restaurant generating $100,000 in average monthly revenue that expects to operate at 60 percent of its normal sales volume during a two-month renovation. Under that hypothetical scenario, the restaurant would experience approximately $80,000 in revenue reduction compared with its normal sales levels. That figure does not represent an equivalent loss in profit, since certain variable expenses may also decline. However, fixed obligations such as rent, insurance, and some payroll costs may continue. Restaurant owners should estimate how construction will affect both revenue and expenses before committing to a renovation schedule. Whenever possible, owners may benefit from scheduling improvements during historically slower periods or completing construction in phases. Evaluate the Expected Return Not every renovation produces an immediate increase in revenue. Some improvements are necessary to maintain safety, replace aging equipment, or preserve the restaurant’s appearance. Others may be intended to increase seating capacity, improve kitchen efficiency, or attract additional customers. Before investing, owners should distinguish between operational necessities and improvements expected to generate measurable financial returns. articles.title: Major Wendy’s Franchisee Significantly Cuts Footprint During Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: Major Wendy’s Franchisee Significantly Cuts Footprint During Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Wendy's franchisee declared bankruptcy in September. Large Wendy’s franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group has closed 33 Wendy’s restaurants since filing for bankruptcy in September, with another 20–60 shutdowns required by November 13 under a court-approved agreement. The company had already closed approximately 60 underperforming Wendy’s restaurants before bankruptcy, beginning in Q4 2025. Meritage estimated those earlier closures would improve annual EBITDA by $8 million. According to Meritage, these locations were losing money, and shedding their leases and franchise agreements would eliminate unnecessary expenses. The franchisee filed for bankruptcy on September 17 . At filing, it operated 320 restaurants across 15 states, including 314 Wendy’s, and employed approximately 8,850 people. Wendy’s moved to terminate Meritage’s franchise agreements one day before the bankruptcy filing and claims the operator owes roughly $146.9 million in royalties, fees, and other contractual charges. Meritage disputes the termination’s effectiveness and maintains its franchise agreements are still in place. Meritage’s financial troubles intensified over the past two years. Same-store sales fell 7.2 percent in fiscal 2025 and another 8.3 percent during the first half of 2026. The company reported net losses of $31.5 million and $23.1 million during those periods, respectively. The operator attributed its difficulties to weak sales, elevated beef costs, national discounting, disruptive weather, and what it described as less effective Wendy’s marketing under prior brand officials. Before bankruptcy, Meritage pursued cost reductions, changes to breakfast service, and sale-leaseback transactions to improve profitability and reduce debt. Urbane Cafe is growing its Central Coast presence with its new Goleta location, bringing its take on fresh, made-from-scratch dining to the broader Santa Barbara area. Known for its house-baked focaccia, gourmet sandwiches and signature bowls, the California-born brand will welcome guests at its newest location on Monday, October 26. Since opening its doors in Ventura in 2003, Urbane Cafe has set out to make fresh, high-quality food a staple of the fast-casual experience. The brand’s menu features focaccia baked from scratch every day, gourmet sandwiches paired with fresh side salads, hearty bowls and house-made sauces. Each location is an open scratch kitchen with a signature hearth oven, where guests can watch their meals come together. “We love the Central Coast and are excited to bring our scratch-made menu to Goleta,” said Tom Holt, Founder of Urbane Cafe. “The Santa Barbara community has been inquiring about a location for a long time – and we are thrilled that we are able to officially be a part of their amazing community. Their enthusiasm means a lot to us and we look forward to serving them for years to come.” To mark the Goleta debut, Urbane Cafe will celebrate with a lineup of grand opening offerings for community members to enjoy: Grand Opening Day (October 26): The first 50 guests in line will receive a free sandwich every month for a year (12 sandwiches total). A ribbon-cutting ceremony with the Santa Barbara South Coast Chamber of Commerce will take place at 10 a.m. Student Giveback Day (October 28): Students can enjoy a complimentary sandwich, salad or bowl when they order through the Urbane Cafe app with a promotional code. Students must sign up here in advance to receive the code and present a valid student ID at pickup. Limited to 500 Students. Teacher Giveback Day (November 4): Teachers and school staff can enjoy a complimentary sandwich, salad or bowl by completing the RSVP form here to receive a promotional code and placing an online order. This opening comes on the heels of opening the first-ever location in Glendale in September, furthering the brand’s ambitious growth goals. Urbane Cafe plans to open six new Southern California locations in 2027, with a long-term target of 100 total locations by 2030. Building on its active growth into Las Vegas and Arizona, the brand continues to prioritize strategic expansion while preserving the food quality, guest experience and company culture that have defined Urbane Cafe since its founding. Great Place To Work and Fortune magazine have selected White Castle for the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail list. This is White Castle’s fifth consecutive year being named to this prestigious list, this year coming in at 11 th place in the large category. Earning a spot means that White Castle is one of the best retail companies to work for in the country. The Best Workplaces in Retail award is based on analysis of survey responses from nearly 76,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the retail industry. “From our founding in 1921, my great-grandfather Billy Ingram dedicated his leadership to creating a workplace where people are respected, valued and supported,” said John Kelley, chief people officer and fourth-generation family member. “And in the 105 years since, we’ve never wavered on that commitment. It’s an honor to be recognized as a one of the very Best Workplaces in Retail, and we share this recognition with every one of our nearly 9,000 team members.” The Best Workplaces in Retail list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America’s largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on over 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 7.3 million employees. Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, work status, or other demographic identifier. “Congratulations to the Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail,” says Michael C. Bush, CEO of Great Place To Work. “People are at the heart of work in every industry, and retail is no exception. These companies show how delivering for your people drives financial performance and turns fear of the future into the confidence to win.” White Castle is widely recognized for its family-centered culture and team member growth. Tropical Smoothie Cafe, one of the nation’s leading fast-casual restaurant brands, has announced a 40-unit franchise development deal across New York and Connecticut with franchisee Aurify Kingstar, expanding the brand’s presence in key Northeast markets. The agreement marks a significant step in Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s next phase of strategic franchise growth. With more than 1,750 cafes and a robust development pipeline, the brand is on track to open its 1,800th location by the end of 2026. As part of its continued investment in franchise development, Tropical Smoothie Cafe recently appointed Joe Sieve as Chief Development & Growth Officer to lead the brand’s development strategy and growth initiatives. The deal will expand Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s presence across Albany, Westchester County, the Bronx, and Western Connecticut, with Aurify Kingstar planning to open its first location in early 2027. “New York and Connecticut represent tremendous growth opportunities for Tropical Smoothie Cafe and reflect the potential ahead as we enter our next phase of growth,” said Max Wetzel, CEO of Tropical Smoothie Cafe, LLC. “Aurify Kingstar brings the restaurant experience, infrastructure, and proven multi-unit development capabilities we look for in growth partners. Together, we can meaningfully expand our presence in the Northeast while continuing to deliver the guest experience and community connection that define our brand.” Andy Stern, John Rigos, and Jeremy Tannenbaum spearhead Aurify Kingstar’s development efforts, bringing more than 25 years of experience building and operating restaurant concepts. Throughout their careers, the team has developed their own concepts and built a diverse franchise portfolio, gaining extensive expertise in restaurant operations, brand development, and multi-unit growth. “We’ve followed Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s growth and success for some time, and the strength of the brand and the experience it creates for guests stood out to us,” said Tannenbaum. “As operators, we’re passionate about restaurant concepts that bring people together and become part of the communities they serve. We see a tremendous opportunity to build Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s presence throughout the Northeast, create great experiences for our guests, and establish meaningful connections in each community we enter.” As Tropical Smoothie Cafe advances its franchise growth strategy, the brand continues to see strong confidence from both new and existing franchisees while prioritizing experienced developers like Aurify Kingstar, who bring strong market knowledge, established infrastructure, and the ability to scale multi-unit operations. Aurify Kingstar identified Tropical Smoothie Cafe as a strong addition to its portfolio based on the brand’s established system, growing consumer demand, available development whitespace, and continued nationwide growth. For more information about Tropical Smoothie Cafe and its menu offerings, visit TropicalSmoothieCafe.com. With more than 25 years of experience, Julio Sánchez has led operations, franchising, development and transformation across North America, Latin America, the Caribbean and Europe. Pollo Campero, the Guatemalan-born quick-service restaurant known for its fried and roasted chicken, has named industry veteran Julio Sánchez CEO of its U.S. business, effective immediately. The company thanks outgoing chief operating officer Luis Javier Rodas, who concluded nearly 26 years with CMI on Oct. 16, for his contributions to the brand’s growth in the U.S. With more than 25 years of experience, Sánchez has led operations, franchising, development and transformation across North America, Latin America, the Caribbean and Europe. Most recently, he served as chief operating officer of CKE International (Carl’s Jr.), and previously held leadership roles at Pizza Hut, Burger King and Church’s Chicken, where he successfully introduced brands into new markets and drove strong same-store sales growth. As CEO, Sánchez will lead the next phase of profitable growth for Campero USA, initially focusing on improving operational excellence, accelerating same-store sales growth, increasing brand awareness and elevating the guest experience to bring the Campero flavor to even more consumers across the United States. His appointment comes as the brand grows beyond 150 U.S. restaurants and works toward continued U.S. expansion. Known for his hands-on style, Sánchez leads from the restaurant floor, staying close to the team members, franchise partners and guests who shape the experience every day. “Julio combines deep operational expertise with sound business judgment and a proven record of delivering results. He is the right leader to guide Campero into its next stage of growth,” said José Gregorio Baquero, global CEO of CMI Foods. Pollo Campero was founded in Guatemala in 1971 and is part of Corporación Multi Inversiones (CMI), a family-owned company with 106 years of history. “I was immediately drawn to Campero’s heritage, sense of hospitality and, of course, flavor,” said Sánchez. “As we bring Pollo Campero to more communities across the U.S., I’m committed to putting our restaurant team members and guests at the forefront to ensure a memorable experience every time they come to our table.” The post Pollo Campero Names Julio Sánchez CEO of U.S. Segment appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef
articles.titleKo: Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Aria has named Elissa Hayward executive pastry chef, adding another creative voice to a team where ideas already move between the kitchen, pastry, bar, and wine programs. Hayward reunites with executive chef Austin Goetzman, with whom she previously worked at Lazy Betty, and joins bar lead Eric Simpkins and lead sommelier and assistant general manager Princeton Saunders as the group continues developing, tasting, and exchanging ideas across their respective areas. That collaboration is already taking shape. Hayward and Saunders have been tasting wines for a red wine sorbet, and conversations with Simpkins about smoked flavors have connected what is happening in pastry with what’s happening behind the bar. She and Goetzman regularly taste one another’s work, continuing a creative relationship they first developed while working together previously. “Elissa’s approach immediately stood out to us,” says owner Andrés Loaiza. “She understands the entire kitchen, not just one part of it, and that comes through in the way she thinks about dessert. She has a strong technical foundation, but she also brings curiosity and personality to what she creates. We’re excited to give her the room to explore that at Aria.” For Hayward, joining Aria is an opportunity to develop her own style while working alongside a team whose individual specialties often inform one another. “I think what is exciting is that everyone is really immersed in their own area, but we’re still constantly talking and tasting together,” says Hayward. “Austin is focused on the savory menu, Eric and Princeton are bringing new ideas to the bar and wine programs, and I’m focused on pastry. We all have our own areas, but there is a lot of opportunity for those ideas to come together.” An early glimpse of her approach appears in a dessert Hayward is beginning to develop, featuring smoked vanilla mousse (pictured below), green apple, turmeric, brown butter crumble, and caramel. The combination reflects several elements of her style: familiar flavors and classical technique paired with unexpected ingredients, contrasting textures, and a subtle savory influence. Hayward’s path to pastry has shaped the way she approaches dessert. She trained in both culinary arts and baking and pastry, then spent much of her early career on the savory side of the kitchen before choosing to focus fully on pastry several years ago. Her experience includes time at Bouchon Bistro in California and, most recently, The Deer and the Dove in Decatur. That background still influences her work. Hayward gravitates toward French classics and traditional technique, but she is equally interested in texture, unexpected flavors, and the memories certain ingredients can evoke. A dessert might recall fall, a childhood favorite, or time spent around a campfire, then reinterpret that feeling through a more refined lens. “I love the classics, but I also love playing with nostalgia and finding ways to make something feel familiar and new at the same time,” says Hayward. “There can be something playful about the flavors while there is still a lot of technique behind them. That combination is what I’m always drawn to.” At Aria, Hayward wants pastry to carry the same attention to detail as the savory menu while still giving guests a final course that can surprise them. “I’m excited to involve guests in the pastry side of the menu in the same way they experience the savory side,” says Hayward. “I want dessert to feel like part of the complete meal, with just as much thought behind it, while also giving guests something they may not have expected.” The post Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef appeared first on FSR magazine .

Currito, a fast-casual franchise fueling communities through their globally inspired menu, is thrilled to announce its continued growth throughout the Cincinnati area with two newly signed franchise agreements. The brand recently secured a three-unit agreement with Petey Cunningham and his partnership group for restaurants in Mason, Milford and Eastgate, as well as a one-unit agreement with existing franchisee Ketul Patel for a new location in Liberty Township. The Cincinnati agreements are the latest example of a broader development surge for Currito, which has now signed 34 franchise units system-wide over the last 22 months and has fully sold-out development rights in the Lexington, Louisville and Dayton markets. These mark another step forward for Currito as the brand continues to expand through experienced, values-driven operators who believe in its fresh, customizable menu, streamlined operations and people-first approach to franchising. As Currito grows both in new markets and within existing communities, these latest agreements reflect the brand’s ability to attract new restaurant entrepreneurs while also encouraging continued investment from franchisees already in the system. Two Experienced Operators Invest in Currito’s Cincinnati Growth Cunningham will lead development for the three new Cincinnati-area locations. A longtime restaurant industry executive, Cunningham spent the last 17 years with One Holland Group, where he joined as controller in 2008 before advancing to chief financial officer and chief development officer. Throughout his career, he has worked across several restaurant brands and gained experience in accounting, finance, development, and day-to-day restaurant operations. His path into restaurants began while attending Ohio State University and later working at Skyline Chili, where he discovered a passion for hospitality, serving others and building strong teams. “After spending nearly two decades in the restaurant industry, I knew I wanted to build something of my own with the right brand and the right people,” said Cunningham. “Currito checked the boxes we were looking for: simple operations, clean and comfortable restaurants, a product people can feel good about and a leadership team that feels like a true partner. Being able to get to know Joe and John and see how hands-on the Thunderdome team is made this feel less like a traditional franchise agreement and more like joining a family.” Patel, an existing Currito franchisee, will continue his growth with the brand through a new restaurant in Liberty Township. A Certified Public Accountant (CPA) by trade, Patel has previous restaurant ownership experience and operates his Currito business alongside his family, including his brother and their wives, who help run the business day to day. Before becoming a franchisee, Patel was first a loyal Currito customer, eating at the restaurant consistently and becoming impressed by the brand’s ability to deliver the same quality, flavor, and experience every time. “Before I ever became a franchisee, I was a Currito customer for two years, and what stood out to me was the consistency,” said Patel . “Every time I came in, the food quality and experience were the same. That is not always easy to find in restaurants, and it gave me confidence in the brand. Expanding with another location in Liberty Township is a natural next step for our family and our team.” Together, Cunningham and Patel represent two important growth paths for Currito: a new franchisee bringing deep restaurant leadership experience into the system and an existing operator expanding after seeing the brand’s potential firsthand. Applebee's brought back Sizzlin' Skillets for the fall season. Michelle Chin spent her first year as Applebee’s CMO visiting restaurants, meeting franchisees, and watching how employees interacted with their regulars. Some guests had favorite seats. Others called ahead to make sure a particular server would be working. A few employees even considered themselves the mayor of the neighborhood. Those relationships gave Chin a starting point for the brand’s marketing. Applebee’s had spent decades building its identity around being a neighborhood gathering place. Inside its restaurants, she found evidence that the promise still meant something. The task now is translating that experience into a reason to visit, including among younger consumers who have chosen other restaurants or have little familiarity with Applebee’s. She sees opportunity in the occasions surrounding the bigger events on people’s calendars. A family can stop in before a game. Friends can catch up after a movie. Sunday church services can lead to a meal together. None requires a birthday, holiday, or elaborate plan.` “It’s all about that human connection and that socialization at the table where people can have a conversation,” Chin says. “And it could be big conversations, but even more importantly, it’s those little moments. Sure, I would love game days and birthdays and all of that. But I think what’s even more important are those in-between moments. And I’ve been playing with this notion of, really wanting people to get together at Applebee’s on those pre and post moments around the main event and their lives.” That thinking gives Applebee’s a role in everyday life that Chin wants its marketing to communicate more clearly. The restaurant can be an easy place to reconnect, with familiar food and a setting that doesn’t demand much preparation. “I think we’ve put this whole notion of dining out on a pedestal and it makes it hard and kind of like out of touch with it. And so make it casual again. Like I just want to connect. I just want to see you. Let’s just grab some wings,” Chin says. Making that message relevant involves changes across marketing and the menu. During her first year, Chin has added talent, tested products, and increased the brand’s participation in social conversations. Applebee’s also named BBDO Chicago its new creative agency of record, following nearly a decade with Grey. The roster includes new vice presidents of integrated marketing and culinary. Chin sees those positions as important to connecting the brand’s message with what guests actually encounter when they sit down to eat. A social team that came aboard shortly before her arrival has helped Applebee’s listen to customers and identify conversations where it can participate naturally. Chin says the brand has seen traffic gains among Gen Z consumers. The objective is to earn a place in people’s daily conversations without turning every interaction into a product pitch. “When we do jump into the conversation and be part of their everyday conversation, the brand’s showing up authentically,” Chin says. “We’re not trying to hard sell anything. I think the teams have done an amazing job there.” The culinary work starts with categories customers already associate with Applebee’s. Appetizers and burgers provide familiar foundations.
