This holiday season, Whataburger is bringing the heat, the holiday cheer and plenty of bold flavors to the table. Beginning Oct. 20, the Bacon Blaze lineup fires up the menu with the fan-favorite Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double and new Bacon Blaze Chicken, both packing the perfect kick. And for Guests who’d rather sip than sizzle, the Sleigh Berry Whatafresher and the Whataburger White Chocolate Raspberry Shake give Guests two festive ways to satisfy their sweet tooth. The full limited-time lineup includes: Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double – The Bacon Blaze lineup offers just the right amount of heat that never sacrifices flavor. The Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double layers two fresh, 100% beef patties with creamy Jalapeño Ranch, jalapeño cream cheese, smoky bacon, sliced jalapeños and real aged cheddar cheese. Guests looking for a smaller bite can order it in a Jr. size. Bacon Blaze Chicken – The new Bacon Blaze Chicken puts that same perfect kick on premium chicken, with Guests’ choice of grilled or Whatachick’n® on a toasted potato bun. articles.title: Newport Beach’s Sushi Ii Changes Name to Sushi Suhama
articles.titleKo: Newport Beach’s Sushi Ii Changes Name to Sushi Suhama
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sushi Ii, the intimate Japanese restaurant in Newport Beach’s Mariner’s Mile, has entered its next chapter as Sushi Suhama, with a new name that reflects both the restaurant’s Japanese roots and its connection to the coastal landscape it calls home. While the name is new, Sushi Suhama remains an evolution of the restaurant guests have come to know, continuing its commitment to seasonality, craftsmanship, and traditional Japanese culinary technique. The intimate setting and culinary team that have defined the restaurant remain at the heart of Sushi Suhama. Since opening, the restaurant has been recognized by the MICHELIN Guide six times, a distinction Sushi Suhama carries with it into this next chapter. The name Suhama comes from an ancient Japanese term referring to a beautiful or picturesque shoreline. For the restaurant, Suhama evokes the natural shoreline that defines Newport Beach, creating a connection between Japanese culture and the coastal setting that has been part of the restaurant’s identity since opening. Renowned Japanese artist Hiroshi Sugimoto was commissioned to help shape this next chapter and selected the name Sushi Suhama for the restaurant. One of Sugimoto’s celebrated seascapes will also be displayed within the space, further connecting the restaurant’s new identity to the meeting of sea, landscape, and Japanese artistry. “Suhama felt meaningful because it gives the restaurant a sense of place. This is still the restaurant our guests know, but the new name gives us an opportunity to express more clearly who we are today and where we are going, while remaining true to what has always defined the experience,” said Director Natsuko Travioli. Along with the new identity, Sushi Suhama has refined its omakase offerings to give guests distinct ways to experience the restaurant. The Sai Kaiseki Course offers the most expansive progression through the traditions of Japanese multi-course dining, while the new Ran Signature Course balances composed seasonal dishes with a greater emphasis on sushi. The Mio Sushi Course places nigiri at the center of the experience, offering the most sushi-forward expression of the three. The new structure allows guests to choose the style of omakase experience that most appeals to them, from a complete kaiseki progression to an experience centered more heavily around sushi. Across each, menus continue to evolve with the seasons and the availability of ingredients at their peak. The evolution comes under the continued culinary leadership of Chefs Norio Izawa and Koji Takahashi, alongside Director Natsuko Travioli. Izawa heads Sushi Suhama’s kaiseki program, drawing upon his training in respected kaiseki kitchens in Tokyo and Kanazawa and experience at Nobu in New York and Bluefin in Newport Beach to guide the restaurant’s multi-course culinary experience. Takahashi, who has been with the restaurant since its opening and brings nearly four decades of experience to his craft, leads the sushi program. Working alongside him is Chef Tatsushi Wakabayashi, who joined the team approximately a year ago and brings experience from Nobu, Ikko, and Oshima. Together, the chefs preserve the discipline and precision of traditional Japanese cooking while allowing the experience to evolve with a modern sensibility. That philosophy extends beyond the menu. From the ceramics selected for each presentation to the intimate counter experience and considered pace of service, Sushi Suhama remains rooted in the Japanese belief that hospitality is expressed through attention to detail. The restaurant’s new identity builds upon that foundation rather than redefining it, marking a natural evolution of a restaurant that has continued to refine itself since opening. Vicious Biscuit, the original home of unapologetically bold biscuits, has signed veteran restaurant operators Doug Puryear and Brian Smith as franchise partners in South Georgia. The longtime business partners, who own and operate nine Surcheros restaurants, will open their first Vicious Biscuit in Valdosta, with an anticipated spring 2027 opening. The agreement marks Vicious Biscuit’s entry into the market as the Charleston-born fast-casual breakfast and brunch brand continues expanding across the Southeast and Midwest. Puryear and Smith, whose restaurant group operates as SAP Saint Simons, bring 30 years of combined restaurant industry experience to Vicious Biscuit. Puryear has spent 10 years in the business, while Smith has 20 years, including a decade owning two Hardee’s locations. Together, they previously operated two Huddle House restaurants for 10 years. Their Surcheros locations in Valdosta and Brunswick consistently rank among the brand’s top performers. Their interest in Vicious Biscuit began when Puryear visited the brand’s flagship restaurant in Mount Pleasant, SC. Impressed by the food and guest experience, he encouraged Smith to visit. After experiencing the concept firsthand and meeting with Vicious Biscuit’s leadership team, the partners decided to add the brand to their restaurant portfolio. “The food is what initially got our attention, but the more we learned about Vicious Biscuit, the more impressed we became,” said Puryear. “We’ve worked with several restaurant brands over the years, and the operations, technology and support systems Vicious Biscuit has already put in place really stood out. They’ve built a strong foundation, and we wanted to be part of it.” The partners were also attracted to Vicious Biscuit’s single-daypart operating model, which focuses on breakfast and brunch. Having previously operated 24-hour restaurants, they recognized the appeal of a more focused approach to staffing, restaurant operations and the guest experience. “Vicious Biscuit has put a lot of thought into how the business operates,” said Smith. “The leadership team understands what franchisees need, and they’ve built the systems to support them. At the same time, the food and hospitality are what make the brand different. That’s an important combination for us.” The approximately 4,000-square-foot Valdosta restaurant will be located at 3259 Inner Perimeter Road, Suite G, in the North Oak Square Shopping Center, adjacent to the partners’ existing Surcheros restaurant. The restaurant is expected to seat 80 to 90 guests. “Doug and Brian have a proven track record of operating successful restaurants and building strong teams,” said George McLaughlin, co-founder and CEO of Vicious Biscuit. “They’re actively involved in their businesses, understand their markets and share our commitment to great food and hospitality. They’re exactly the kind of experienced operators we want to grow with.” As Vicious Biscuit expands into new markets, the brand continues to invest in franchise training, operational systems and technology to support its single-daypart restaurant model. Vicious Biscuit currently operates 13 restaurants, including seven corporate and six franchise locations, with eight additional franchise units signed and under development. Another 33 restaurants are committed under existing franchise agreements, with development contingent upon securing leases. Ever wondered what makes a Quarter Pounder with Cheese sandwich so craveable? Why the egg on an Egg McMuffin breakfast sandwich is perfectly round? Or what goes into the fries you’ve loved for years? On October 29, fans in New York City can snag a seat and find out for themselves. For one day only, McDonald’s and “Top Chef” Season 22 winner and former McDonald’s Crew member Tristen Epps-Long are opening the doors to Inside the Golden Arches , a complimentary chef’s table experience where fans can hear directly from chefs and experts about the quality ingredients, attention to detail and small touches behind some of McDonald’s most iconic menu items. Stepping into the spotlight is the hot and deliciously juicy Quarter Pounder with Cheese. Guests will see how it’s prepared, from the 100% real beef cooked fresh when ordered to the simple ingredients that make it a fan favorite. They’ll also enjoy other McDonald’s iconic menu items, including the Egg McMuffin, Chicken McNuggets and World Famous Fries. Is your mouth watering yet? Chef Tristen will guide guests through the experience, sharing his perspective as a chef—and as one of the 1 in 8 Americans who have worked behind the counter at McDonald’s. “McDonald’s was where I got my start, and the experience helped shape the way I think about food and hospitality,” said Chef Tristen. “Even now, I have a deep appreciation for the consistency that allows millions of people to enjoy the same great meal wherever they are. Inside the Golden Arches gives fans a rare opportunity to see the people, processes and care behind that experience.” While seats at the table are limited, the Quarter Pounder with Cheese celebration is just getting started. Beginning Nov. 2, fans across the country can enjoy the Quarter Pounder with Cheese complete with medium fries and a drink for just $8, at participating McDonald’s restaurants. “Inside the Golden Arches is about creating a new level of access and transparency for our fans,” said Gina Hardy, Vice President, U.S. Marketing & Menu Strategy. “People know the Quarter Pounder with Cheese as one of McDonald’s most iconic burgers, but they may not know that it’s made with 100% beef, never frozen, delivered to local restaurants 2-3 times a week and grilled once you order. We’re excited to give fans a firsthand look at these quality ingredients and gold standard practices, helping them see what makes McDonald’s uniquely McDonald’s.” READY TO PULL UP A CHAIR? articles.title: Pancheros Plays the Long Game on Value and Growth
articles.titleKo: Pancheros Plays the Long Game on Value and Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Pancheros has around 75 restaurants systemwide. Back to normal. It’s a state of being restaurants have been scratching and clawing for in the years since the pandemic sent shockwaves through the industry. For Pancheros founder and CEO Rodney Anderson, 2026 has proven to be the year that the phrase has actually become real. “We’ve been working really hard and trying to make the unit level economics exactly what they were before the pandemic, and I think we’ve done a great job with that,” Anderson says. The roughly 75-unit Pancheros worked with suppliers to mitigate protein costs and leveraged AI tools to better calculate the right yield amounts and reduce waste. As a result, according to Anderson, Pancheros is back to the lowest food cost it’s ever had, even with continued cost increases related to taxes, digital services, and other expenses. Franchisees appear to be on board with the brand’s direction, especially because of better operations. Pancheros has focused on remodeling older locations with digital make lines, a feature that’s led to increases in overall sales—not just digital. That’s in addition to better customer satisfaction, more efficient throughput, and lower employee turnover. More digital make lines are being added to restaurants each week. “First you say, ‘Well, digital sales should go up, but you don’t realize that the in-restaurant guest really likes being treated properly, and those digital sales and the old design with the single make line were interfering with the in-restaurant experience. So that pain went away,” Anderson says. “…It is great for business. It really helps with those peak periods. And not just in handling the third party and the digital stuff, but handling the overall restaurant and the entire package—the entire experience that the customer has.” The rise in digital sales, which account for about 33 percent of sales, has coincided with increased loyalty membership. This year, Pancheros reached 1 million members, or about 13,500 per location. About 26.17 percent of members actively participate. These guests have access to promotions around National Burrito Day, Cinco de Mayo, Teacher Appreciation, and more. Pancheros plans to offer a Halloween BOGO deal for its loyalty members next week. “During the pandemic, we had a real strategy to push digital. Only a couple weeks into it, we realized that we had to have that pickup and delivery work, and we took our entire budget and canceled a lot of projects, canceled a lot of creative, and we really pushed it into developing digital, and our digital grew like crazy, and it’s really given us an advantage over other restaurant chains,” Anderson says. Anderson describes these promotions as rewarding loyal customers as opposed to discounting. The executive says Pancheros is in an advantageous position because it limited price increases a few years after the pandemic. The chain raised prices no more than 4 percent, he says. So for those brands that may have implemented double-digit price increases, guests are pushing back, according to Anderson. The same isn’t happening for Pancheros because of its willingness to accept lower margins in the short term. “We have kept our prices low. We will probably see a price increase this spring again, probably no more than a few percent. And we just want to treat the customers right, and be concerned with long-run sales and value with them, and not go out and start doing these bundled meals and discounts and things like that,” Anderson says. “But we do have a good loyalty program where we do reward them for eating there, and we do some promotions to bring them in. But we’re just very stable in how we approach the consumer, and we try to respect that long term.” Growth is coming as well. Pancheros has several leases signed, mostly in the Midwest. articles.title: 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant to Debut in Mayfair This November, Marking the Brand’s First UK Opening
articles.titleKo: 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant to Debut in Mayfair This November, Marking the Brand’s First UK Opening
articles.originalSummary: The internationally acclaimed 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant is set to make its UK debut this November with the launch of its newest flagship in London’s Mayfair, introducing a refined, contemporary Japanese dining and bar experience to one of the city’s most prestigious districts. Located at 22 Park Lane, the opening marks a significant milestone for 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant as it enters the UK market for the first time, joining an established international portfolio spanning Madrid, Barcelona, Marbella, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Monaco, Rabat and Budapest. Since its beginnings in Madrid, 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant has developed an international trajectory underpinned by prestigious gastronomic recognition across multiple markets. Its Abu Dhabi restaurant has held a MICHELIN Star for three consecutive years, while both Abu Dhabi and Dubai were awarded One Toque by Gault&Millau in 2024. Most recently, 99 Sushi Bar Rabat was awarded Two Toques by Gault&Millau in 2026, during the guide’s inaugural edition in Morocco. The London opening represents the next chapter in 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant’s continued international expansion, bringing its distinctive approach to contemporary Japanese gastronomy to the capital for the first time. A Contemporary Expression of Japanese Culinary Art 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant Mayfair presents an elegant and modern interpretation of traditional Japanese cuisine, elevated through precise craftsmanship and an uncompromising approach to ingredient sourcing. At the core of its offering is a commitment to premium produce, notably Atlantic fatty bluefin tuna, and a culinary philosophy rooted in near-perfect execution “99% perfect,” reflecting the brand’s belief that absolute perfection remains unattainable. The menu is designed as a journey through refined Japanese gastronomy, subtly infused with European techniques and influences inspired by the travels of founders Pedro and Fernando de León. This fusion creates a distinctive culinary identity that challenges conventional expectations of a traditional sushi restaurant. Design-Led Dining and Immersive Atmosphere The Mayfair venue has been conceived as an urban lifestyle destination, combining sophisticated design with immersive sensory detail. Interiors feature gold accents, mirrored surfaces, amber-lit textures and rich velvet tones in purple and crimson, creating an intimate and atmospheric dining environment. The restaurant also includes landscaped outdoor terraces featuring sculptural bonsai installations that reinterpret Japanese garden symbolism through a contemporary lens, offering guests a striking contrast between nature and urban London. Dining Spaces & Capacity The restaurant accommodates a variety of experiences across a series of distinct spaces: ● Dining Area – Capacity: up to 60 guests ● Cabaret Bar – Capacity: 19 guests, 21+ only ● Sushi Counter – Capacity: 4 guests, offering chef-led counter dining with live preparation Total capacity reaches 85 seated guests, with up to 185 guests for cocktail receptions, making the venue equally suited to private events and brand activations. Brand Story and Award Recognition Founded in Madrid in 2005 by brothers Fernando and Pedro de León, 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant has grown from a pioneering Japanese dining concept into an internationally recognised hospitality brand. Built on a passion for Japanese culinary heritage, innovation and a constant pursuit of excellence, the group is now entering its next phase of global growth under Group CEO Jaime Castañeda, who brings more than 18 years of international hospitality experience and has led the brand’s accelerated expansion across Europe and the GCC. With a MICHELIN Star in Abu Dhabi for three consecutive years, 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant continues to strengthen its international reputation. 99 Sushi Bar Dubai has also been awarded One Toque by Gault&Millau, while 99 Sushi Bar Rabat received Two Toques from Gault&Millau in 2026, during the guide’s inaugural edition in M

articles.title: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.titleKo: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far

Dakota Hotel Group’s stylish, luxury hotel welcomed over 15,000 guests in the opening 100 days, including new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. Guests range from business travellers staying ahead of early morning domestic flights, alongside leisure guests heading to destinations across the globe. Recent guests have travelled on to New York, Los Angeles, Barbados, Singapore and Bangkok, as well as domestic and European routes. The hotel offers a luxury experience with ultimate comfort, to ensure travellers get a great night’s sleep before embarking on their journeys around the globe. Dakota Manchester Airport has seen strong demand throughout the week, with Thursdays and Fridays proving to be particularly busy as guests set off on long weekend breaks or prepare for early flights. The hotel’s parking packages have been extremely popular from the outset. Guests appreciate the convenience of leaving their vehicle at the hotel and being transferred directly to their airport terminal in comfort by Dakota’s concierge team. It also provides guests with the added reassurance of knowing their vehicle is parked in a secure hotel environment while they are away. It’s not just air travellers that are visiting Manchester Airport’s new luxury hotel, local residents and businesses have been enjoying the hotel’s stylish food and beverage offerings alongside hotel residents. At the heart of the hotel sits The Grill where the menu reflects true Dakota style, centering on bold, flavour-led dishes made with high-quality produce and generous portions. There are premium steaks, indulgent sides, and a carefully curated wine list, delivering a memorable dining experience. Steak has long been at the heart of the Dakota table, and the 28-day dry-aged fillet remains the best-selling dish across every Dakota restaurant, Manchester Airport included. Truffle Parmesan Fries and Tenderstem Broccoli sautéed in Garlic, Chilli and Soy are the most popular accompaniments, and Dakota’s signature Sticky Toffee Pudding, served in a rich butterscotch sauce with Madagascan Vanilla Ice Cream continues to be the dessert of choice. Many guests choose to start their holiday with a glass of Taittinger Champagne, making it a popular choice for celebrations and special occasions. In The Bar, the Hugo Spritz, Classic Margarita and a range of brunch-favourite cocktails continue to be among the best-selling drinks, helping guests relax and begin their travels in style. Matt Townley, Group Operations Director, said: “With Dakota Manchester Airport, we’re bringing something different to the airport market, combining the luxury, style and service that our guests know and trust with the convenience of an airport location. articles.title: The Langham, London Reveals ‘The Winter Garden’ for the Festive Season
articles.titleKo: The Langham, London Reveals ‘The Winter Garden’ for the Festive Season
articles.originalSummary: This Christmas, The Langham, London will transform into ‘The Winter Garden’, an elegant festive experience inspired by the beauty of a winter garden. For 2026, London’s original grand hotel will be brought to life with frosted botanicals, sculptural branches, crystal and glass details, and starry lighting. Designed to evolve from day into evening, the design combines luminous winter whites with deeper, warming tones, to create a sense of discovery throughout the property. At the heart of the experience, the Lobby will bloom into a grand Winter Garden, guiding guests to Palm Court for the hotel’s celebrated afternoon tea. In Palm Court, guests can take in ‘The Blooming Winter Garden’, inspired by the Victorian glasshouses that allowed exotic plants and fruits to flourish throughout winter. The Winter Garden Festive Afternoon Tea (available 9 November 2026 to 3 January 2027) will feature seasonal flavours, with finger sandwiches such as Roast Bronze Turkey, stu1ing, pickled cranberries and chestnut with a delicate savoury of Potato farl, crème fraiche and oscietra caviar. Snowy white throughout, with bright pops of colour, the cakes and pastries will showcase the likes of Plum and Ginger and Chestnut and Blackcurrant, all in which will be served alongside scones with clotted cream, preserves, a showstopping sharing cake, alongside The Langham’s Glasshouse; an Earl Grey infused layered sponge with bergamot jelly. As day turns to night, ‘Midnight in the Winter Garden’ will see Artesian cocktail bar transformed into a shimmering evening setting inspired by the season. Head Bartender Giulia Cuccurullo and the talented team at Artesian have created two exclusive festive cocktails for the occasion, the Pineapple & Brioche, a decadent take on the Ramos Gin Fizz, combining caramelised rum with bright pineapple and citrus, balanced by rich brioche notes and finished with a velvety foam and the Fig & Port, a luxurious cocktail inspired by the Manhattan, pairing crisp vodka with rich fig and warming aged port, lifted by the dry, saline character of fino sherry. Guests can also choose to explore the festive cocktails alongside Artesian’s elevated bar snacks menu; perfect for predinner bites or a light supper. For those looking to settle into a cosy space, The Wigmore, The Langham’s modern British pub, will grow into ‘The Evergreen Garden’, o^ering a warm and welcoming embrace for the winter season. Guests can choose from the extensive a la carte menu featuring the likes of Roast Turkey Pie, or opt for festive sharing platters such as The Wigmore Favourites Platter, consisting of XXL stovetop 3 cheese and mustard toastie, fat chips and Bloody Mary salt, buttered crumpets, citrus cured salmon and crème fraiche. Hearty dishes made with seasonal ingredients will be served alongside the festive drinks we all crave as the temperature drops. The celebrations continue across The Langham, London on New Year’s Eve, with a choice of three ways to see out 2026 in style. In Palm Court, guests can enjoy an elegant five-course dinner, beginning with Champagne and canapés and accompanied by live music throughout the evening. At Artesian, celebrations step up from 8pm to enjoy an evening of exceptional cocktails, festive atmosphere and late-night glamour accompanied by the delicious bar snack menu and a live DJ taking guests through to midnight. For something more relaxed, The Wigmore is hosting two sittings to choose from, enjoy an early three-course dinner with English sparkling wine, or settle in for a later dinner and celebration with festive punch, live music and a glass of Champagne to see in the countdown.

articles.title: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.titleKo: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.originalSummary: For more than 25 years, OpenTable has worked alongside restaurants to help them fill tables, connect with diners and grow their businesses. Its 2026 Restaurant Impact Report explores the vital role restaurants play in local economies, communities and everyday life, as well as how diners can help them thrive. The findings demonstrate that restaurants contribute far more than dining alone. They drive spending and footfall for surrounding businesses while creating spaces where people can come together and reconnect. The report explores the challenges restaurants face, including the impact of no-shows, and how small actions from diners can make a meaningful difference. Among the findings: Dining out has an economic ripple effect: 56% of UK diners spend at neighbouring businesses before or after their meal, spending an average of £95. Restaurants bring people together: 98% say local restaurants are important to their community, while 71% of Gen Z diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better or reconnect when they feel stressed or low. Supporting restaurants goes beyond the bill: Among Gen Z diners who made a restaurant reservation in the past year, 57% admit to having failed to show up at least once. A no-show for a table of two costs £55.70 on average, according to restaurant workers,² while 48% say understanding the financial impact of a no-show would make them more likely to honour or cancel a booking. “Restaurants are so much more than places to eat, they create jobs, bring people together and play an important role in the life of communities across the UK,” explains Sasha Shaker, Senior Director of Restaurant Sales and Service, OpenTable UK and Ireland . “This report showcases the industry’s wider impact and highlights why restaurants matter and why OpenTable is dedicated to advocating for their success.” Restaurants Fuel Employment and Local Economies More than half (56%) of UK restaurant diners said they spent money on other activities the last time they ate out locally.¹ Those who spent elsewhere alongside their meal spent £95.20 on average, rising to £126 among Gen Z and £118 among Millennials.¹ Restaurants see this impact first-hand, with 51% of hospitality workers saying their restaurant drives footfall or spending at nearby businesses. According to UKHospitality, hospitality is the UK’s third-largest employer, with restaurants employing 1.3 million people and contributing £44 billion to the economy annually. Restaurants Drive Community and Personal Wellbeing Restaurants provide spaces where people meet, celebrate and connect. More than half (56%) of UK diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better when stressed or low, rising to 71% among Gen Z diners.¹ If their favourite local restaurant disappeared tomorrow, 53% would miss the atmosphere and character it brings. Dr Martha Newson, Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of Greenwich , explains: “Sharing a meal at a restaurant is one of the oldest ways of bringing people together, because sitting around a table lets us focus on each other. Our research with over 10,000 people worldwide found face-to-face contact remains a strong predictor of wellbeing, as social bonds deepen through eye contact and shared experiences.” The Balancing Act for Restaurants While restaurants support their local areas, they are also navigating significant pressures. OpenTable’s research found that if VAT were reduced from 20% and restaurants passed the savings on through lower menu prices, 39% of diners would eat out more often, while a further 22% would spend more when they did. The report also explores how restaurants could use potential VAT savings. According to the research, 42% would primarily use a reduction to protect or increase staff wages and hours, 31% would lower menu prices for customers and 30% would reduce how often they need to raise prices. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. Watching elders transform simple, fresh ingredients into a banquet of rich flavours – and seeing the joy it brought to loved ones – deeply moved him. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. Chef Lau’s career in Cantonese gastronomy spans leading hospitality brands including The Hong Kong Bankers Club, Hong Kong Parkview and the Clearwater Bay Golf & Country Club. He honed his expertise at the Chinese Culinary Institute under the Vocational Training Council, completing advanced master classes and the Master Chef Course in Chinese Cuisine, where he was honoured as Outstanding Trainee of the 10th programme. articles.title: Brad Christian Joins Serve First as Managing Partner to Lead U.S. Expansion
articles.titleKo: Brad Christian Joins Serve First as Managing Partner to Lead U.S. Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Serve First , the operational excellence platform for customer experience across multi-location service businesses, today announced the expansion of its US operations. Brad Christian joins as Managing Director and will lead Serve First in the US from its office in Alpharetta, GA. Brad brings more than 20 years of experience working with clients in the customer experience industry. He was previously Chief Customer Officer at a customer experience consultancy and Chief Commercial Officer for the experience practice of a global market research firm. He has helped brands design and deploy measurement systems that drive strategic insight and deliver real business performance improvement. The US office supports the global expansion of existing client programs. Serve First is building US customer success and marketing teams to serve those and other US-based clients. Brad will work with brands across restaurants, hotels and hospitality, convenience stores and retail petroleum, and facilities management. Most US operators already measure plenty, through surveys, audits, mystery shops and review tracking. The problem is that many times nothing changes at the location because of it. The report arrives next month, and the site manager never sees it. Serve First captures every signal in one platform, from guest feedback and audits to mystery shopping. EVA, the analyst built into the platform, measures each location against the brand’s own standards, finds where it falls short and why, and builds the plan to fix it. The fix goes to the person who can make it, with proof it got done. “Traditional CX programs have many times been more of an academic exercise than a true focus on actually impacting the customer experience,” said Brad Christian, Managing Director, Serve First. “These programs have been optimized for collecting data, but they lack the actionability to drive meaningful change at the front line. Metrics matter, but meaning matters more. When teams have the feedback, the right tasks and the support to change how they work, brands deliver better customer experiences.” “Brad knows what it takes to turn customer experience programs into real change at every location,” said Erol Ayvaz, CEO, Serve First. “Expanding our US operations under his leadership is the next step in Serve First’s global growth, and it gives our US clients a team on the ground.” The post Brad Christian Joins Serve First as Managing Partner to Lead U.S. Expansion appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: 5 Lessons in Leadership from WiRL Keynote Speaker Meg Farren
articles.titleKo: 5 Lessons in Leadership from WiRL Keynote Speaker Meg Farren
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Meg Farren’s path to president of Taco Bell North America ran through JPMorgan, strategy consulting, luxury desserts, grocery retail, and a decade at KFC, where she led a brand turnaround. Then came her biggest move yet: a transatlantic relocation with her family to lead one of the most beloved brands in the world. In a conversation with QSR magazine earlier this year , she reflected on what she has learned along the way. Listen before you lead When Farren started at Taco Bell, she skipped the big pronouncements and went on a listening tour, traveling with second- and third-generation franchisees and learning from managers. “Sometimes you see people come into a new role and feel like they have to prove themselves by telling others what they should be doing,” Farren says. “But the heart of great trust and collaboration is an ability to listen really well and slowly start to say, ‘Have we tried this?’” Registration is now open for Year 4 of the Women in Restaurant Leadership Summit! Bring your whole self to work Farren doesn’t pretend the juggle isn’t real, and she doesn’t expect her team to either. Instead, she tries to create space for openness and vulnerability, starting with her own. “I am a whole person, not just a work person, and most people are juggling the same kinds of trade-offs and priorities at home that I am,” Farren says. “I try to be a role model to my team that yes, we’re all trying to make our lives work.” Stay healthily dissatisfied Taco Bell can turn a great idea around in two weeks, which is rare for a company of its size. Farren credits a culture that never settles and isn’t afraid to disrupt the status quo through thoughtful innovation. “Taco Bell operates like an $18 billion startup, and to execute brilliantly at our size requires a certain culture and level of partnership across the entire business,” Farren says. “There is this constant healthy dissatisfaction with the status quo, and every franchisee can tell you that we are relentlessly innovating for the next generation of growth.” Never underestimate a thank-you To Farren, culture isn’t a corporate slogan. It’s a set of daily behaviors, shaped at every level of the organization in ways seen and unseen, and recognition is one of the most powerful. “You don’t always show up in your best form every day,” Farren says, “but I do try to make sure all voices are heard in the room, that I foster a culture of recognition, and I’m saying ‘thank you’ and recognizing the contributions of others.” Take the big leap, even when life is messy Farren spent six months commuting from London while her kids finished the school year, building relationships over Zoom while managing what she calls “life admin” and big emotions. “I was getting to know a new organization and learning how to navigate these relationships while driving great performance and delivering well for your team and customers—all while managing a huge family transition,” Farren reflects. “I have depths of resilience, and I’ve been lucky to land with a team who cares about me … it’s been a big step up, but totally worth it.” Hear more from Farren live in Scottsdale. She will deliver the afternoon keynote at WiRL 2027, Feb. 7-9, 2027, at the Grand Hyatt Scottsdale Resort, alongside fellow keynoters Nivera Wallani and Amy Ellis Durini of KFC. WiRL has sold out three years running, and registrations are outpacing every previous year. Save your seat here. For guests who make the most of Halloween night, Chipotle has November 1 covered with $0 delivery fees on digital orders. Some Halloween traditions are worth keeping. Boorito is back. For more than 25 years, fans of Chipotle Mexican Grill have dressed up in costume and shown up for Boorito. The fan-favorite Chipotday — the brand’s term for the food holidays and cultural moments it celebrates throughout the year, returns to participating Chipotle restaurants across the U.S. on October 31. Fans know the drill. The rules are frighteningly simple: Wear a costume. Visit Chipotle after 3 p.m. local time on Halloween. Scan your Chipotle Rewards member card at checkout. Score a $6 entrée. 1 For guests who make the most of Halloween night, Chipotle has November 1 covered with $0 delivery fees on digital orders. 2 “We love that Chipotle has become part of so many fans’ Halloween traditions,” said Stephanie Perdue, Senior Vice President, Brand Marketing. “The passion around Boorito inspires us to find new ways to celebrate and surprise our fans year after year.” Boorito Lore 2000 – Boorito began as a burrito-themed costume contest. 2020 – Boorito went fully digital for the first time, inviting fans to virtually trick-or-treat for BOGO codes. 2021 – Boorito entered the metaverse with a virtual Chipotle restaurant. 2023 – Boorito expanded with late-night hours in select college towns. 2024 – Chipotle introduced meme-inspired costumes. 2026 – Chipotle summoned the return of its $6 margaritas in select cities leading up to Boorito 2026. 1 – Chipotle Rewards members can receive one (1) entrée item for US$6 when appearing in costume, as determined by restaurant, and scanning for Rewards at point of sale at participating U.S. locations. Valid only on October 31, 2026 after 3:00 p.m. local time through restaurant closing; redemption is subject to availability. Limit one discounted item per costumed guest. Redeemable in-restaurant only; not valid for kids meals, catering, mobile, online or delivery orders. Extra cost for guacamole (except for veggie entreés), queso, extra meat or other modifiers. Taxes, gratuities, and any sides are not included and are the responsibility of the guest. Purchased entrées are eligible for Chipotle Rewards points; the promotion may not otherwise be combined with other coupons, promotions, or special offers. Additional restrictions may apply; void where prohibited. 2 – Higher menu prices are charged for delivery; additional service and other fees applied at checkout as well (except in CA, CO, CT, MA, MN and VA). Available only on November 1, 2026, within Chipotle’s delivery areas from participating U.S. locations, during normal operating hours for such locations. Minimum order $10 USD excluding tax and fees; maximum item numbers apply as well. Deliveries and redemptions are subject to availability. Offer is not valid on catering or Burritos by the Box orders. Redemptions of Chipotle Rewards and other promotional offers may be included in a qualifying delivery order but do not count towards satisfaction of minimum purchase requirements. Valid only on the Chipotle website or the Chipotle app; not valid on orders placed via third-party delivery platforms. Chipotle reserves the right to modify or terminate this offer at any time without notice. Additional restrictions may apply; void where prohibited. From Strawberry Dragonfruit, Black Tea, Mango and Lemonade, Tractor’s flavors have been a staple at Brooklyn Water Bagel since 2023. The drinks are built on USDA-certified organic ingredients and distinctive flavor, with new rotating options available throughout the year. “We’ve built Brooklyn Water Bagel by being intentional about what we serve, from the water that gives our bagels their signature character to the ingredients across our menu,” said Dan Smith, CEO of Brooklyn Water Bagel. “Tractor shares that approach, with products that stand on their own while complementing the food our fans come to us for. This is a meaningful expansion of our menu and another way we’re raising the bar across the Brooklyn Water Bagel experience.” Tractor Beverage Company creates refreshing items specifically for foodservice brands, with a portfolio spanning fountain drinks, lemonades, teas and specialty beverages. That focus made Tractor a natural fit for Brooklyn Water Bagel. “Bagels and coffee may be what put Brooklyn Water Bagel on the map, but the beverage occasion doesn’t have to stop there,” said Clay Lichterman, Senior Vice President of Foodservice Sales at Tractor. “Our partnership gives the brand a broader beverage platform built around the things today’s guests increasingly care about: organic ingredients, recognizable flavors and drinks that are worth choosing on their own.” The bagel brand’s New York-inspired menu includes hand-rolled sourdough bagels, protein-rich and gluten-free options, Brooklyn Bites, sandwiches, superfood avocado toast and its signature Cubsta iced coffee. With Tractor’s lineup now available at most locations, guests have additional options throughout the day, from a morning tea or lemonade to an afternoon pick-me-up. For more information or to find a location, visit brooklynwaterbagel.com. The post Brooklyn Water Bagel Champions Partnership with Tractor Beverage Company appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Cheba Hut to Open in South Scottsdale, Arizona
articles.titleKo: Cheba Hut to Open in South Scottsdale, Arizona
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A fresh place to grab a bite, kick back with a cold drink and stay awhile is headed to South Scottsdale. Cheba Hut “Toasted” Subs , the counter-culture sandwich shop known for its chill atmosphere, cottonmouth cures, and bold flavors that hit just right, arrives Oct. 26, planted at 2200 N. Scottsdale Road, Suite 110, south of Oak Street and north of McDowell Road. Just south of Old Town Scottsdale, with its world-class shopping, buzzing nightlife, major events and tightly packed arts scene, the restaurant sits close to some of the region’s go-to outings. Guests can fuel up before visiting the Phoenix Zoo, swing by after exploring Papago Park, stop in on the way to Scottsdale Stadium during Cactus League season or make a side quest out of browsing The Antique Trove, Scottsdale Pawn Shop and Sidewalk Surfer Skate Shop. South Scottsdale marks the 13 th Cheba Hut in the Phoenix area and the latest milestone in a fast run for franchise owners Justin and Michelle Lemos, who now operate five shops in less than two years. They launched in North Scottsdale in February 2025, followed with the 101 and Shea a month later, additionally taking over Paradise Valley from Cheba Hut headquarters in January and adding Arcadia in June. “Long before we owned a Cheba Hut, we were regulars who came in for the best sandwich we’d ever had and stuck around for the music, the art and a crew that actually loved being there,” said Justin Lemos, franchise owner. “Those folks are still what it’s all about for us. We promote from within and hire locally, so every opening creates a path for someone on our team to step into something bigger. South Scottsdale means more homegrown careers taking root right alongside the subs.” Like every destination across the Chebaverse, the location tells a local story on its walls. Joshua Finley, who has left his mark on more than 50 Cheba Hut locations nationwide, reimagining the surrounding Old Town “village” as a scene straight out of an anime series. Additional Cheba Hut references fill the frame, along with Easter eggs that reward a second look (and maybe a third). Beyond the centerpiece mural, the space doubles as a showcase for Valley creators, featuring work by pop cannabis artist Aubri Swell ( @MaryJaneArtCompany ) and wood artist Basile Taylor ( @BasileMakesThings ). The owners plan to extend that spotlight to more makers and artisans, with original art for sale so fans can take a little piece of Cheba home. Behind the counter, a full-service bar pours liquor, beer and wine from shelves meant to keep changing. The team will keep adding bottles and taps based on Arizona favorites and crowd requests, so the lineup grows right alongside the neighborhood. For first-timers, Cheba Hut serves more than 30 signature toasted subs named for classic strains and available in Nug (4-inch), Pinner (8-inch) and Blunt (12-inch) sizes. Regulars reach for the White Widow, stacked with chicken, bacon and ranch. The Kali Mist turns up the heat on a club piled with turkey, pepper jack and more of that bacon. The Dank layers pepperoni, salami, marinara and melted mozzarella into a pizza-inspired build, and the Griefo goes green with cream cheese, avocado and fresh vegetables. For something beyond the main event, the menu has plenty of options built for late-night cravings, from pretzel nugs and garlic cheese bread to Krispy Bars, goo balls and cookies, plus the Kool-Aid that’s been quenching thirst since day one. Cheba Hut South Scottsdale will be open Sunday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., with extended hours until midnight Friday and Saturday. With its mix of toasted sandwiches, unserious humor, neighborhood-first mindset and a disrespectful mascot named “Flip the Bird,” Cheba Hut is ready to make Scottsdale a little more dank, one sub at a time. articles.title: Maine’s White Barn Inn Welcomes Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr
articles.titleKo: Maine’s White Barn Inn Welcomes Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . From a working barn to celebrated culinary destination, White Barn Inn, Auberge Collection has spent more than five decades evolving alongside the landscape that surrounds it. Once home to livestock, horses and chickens – and later used as an ice creamery – the historic barn was restored in 1973 and transformed into White Barn Inn Restaurant, establishing a legacy of elevated dining rooted in Maine’s agricultural and coastal bounty. This autumn, the acclaimed restaurant enters a new culinary chapter under Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr, whose international fine-dining career brings a distinctly European perspective to the New England landmark. German-born, Sühr has worked in some of the world’s most acclaimed kitchens, including Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester and The Savoy in London, and later at The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel in New York, where she became the hotel’s first female Chef de Cuisine. She went on to lead kitchens at Jean-Georges Philadelphia at Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia, before joining The Surf Club Restaurant by Thomas Keller in Florida. Now, taking the helm at White Barn Inn, Auberge Collection, Sühr is translating years of classical training and global experience through the lens of coastal Maine, allowing the landscape and its changing seasons to dictate the menu. As autumn settles over Maine, the signature Coast Line & Forest tasting menu evolves to reflect the season, tracing a progression from the coastline to the deeper flavors of land, smoke, and fire. Drawing on Maine’s farms, waters, and forests, Sühr uses techniques including fermentation, preservation, smoking, and live-fire cooking to bring depth and character to ingredients at their peak. The menu continues to evolve with seasonal availability, allowing each harvest to shape the experience. Priced at $250 per guest, with an optional $125 wine pairing, the current menu features: Halibut | Razor Clams | Potato | Dill This dish captures the character of Maine’s coastline while incorporating the elegance of classical French cooking. The halibut offers natural sweetness and a delicate, flaky texture, while the razor clams bring subtle brininess and a slightly firmer bite. Potato adds an earthy, comforting element suited to the fall season, while dill provides freshness and a gentle aromatic lift. The sauce draws inspiration from traditional French moules marinières , using shellfish, white wine, and aromatics to create depth without detracting from the purity of the fish. The result strikes a balance between simplicity and refinement, bringing together familiar coastal New England ingredients through a delicate, contemporary interpretation of French technique that allows the natural flavors of the sea to remain the focus. Stonington Lobster | Parisian Gnocchi | Sea Beans | Fennel Sourcing lobster from Stonington, known as one of Maine’s premier lobster fishing towns, is particularly special. With its deeply rooted fishing heritage, the small coastal community represents much of what makes Maine’s culinary identity unique: tradition, craftsmanship, and a close connection to the sea. Stonington lobster is prized for its natural sweetness and beautiful texture, with succulent, tender meat that retains a delicate firmness and almost buttery richness. Parisian gnocchi introduces a light, airy texture that contrasts beautifully with the lobster, while sea beans bring a crisp bite and subtle ocean salinity. Fennel adds freshness and gentle anise notes. The sauce draws inspiration from a traditional Provençal bourride , lending silky, velvety richness that enhances the lobster’s natural sweetness without overpowering it. The dish brings together two coastal traditions: Stonington’s fishing heritage and the elegance of southern French cuisine. articles.title: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.titleKo: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/

Chang’s. “That’s what I’ve carried through to P.F. Chang’s,” she says. “The question here is, how do we build something that goes beyond our food? How do we create a community and that emotional storytelling component that keeps people coming back and supporting us? Those little moments where you can be involved with your community make your marketing so much stronger, and your brand so much stronger.” There, she approaches marketing as a sequence: It starts with a strong menu, followed by a compelling story that draws guests in, then operational execution and interactive touches in the dining room. It’s a fully integrated approach that spans every channel, but it all starts with the brief. Join women leaders at WiRL! Reserve your spot today. That approach is part of a broader resurgence at P.F. Chang’s . Under CEO Jim Mazany and chief marketing officer Holly Smith, who joined in January, the chain posted a 7.7 percent same-store sales gain in the second quarter, with traffic up 6.8 percent. “Holly and I sat down and thought to ourselves: How do we create something that’s uniquely ownable to P.F. Chang’s?” Bunting says. “How do we tie it back to something culturally relevant that only we can own?” Working with brand manager Olivia Liu, the team built 2026 around a series of seasonal campaigns inspired by Japanese culture. It started in February with Flavor In Bloom , a nod to Japan’s cherry blossom season that paired best-sellers like Chang’s Lettuce Wraps with spring cocktails, led by a Cherry Blossom Martini. articles.title: Harlem Shake Signs 75-Unit Master Franchise Agreement in India
articles.titleKo: Harlem Shake Signs 75-Unit Master Franchise Agreement in India
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The award-winning and critically acclaimed Harlem Shake announces a strategic partnership with Franchise India , and advisory support from FranGlobal, the international arm of Franchise India. The partnership marks a new chapter in the brand’s international expansion, with a Master Franchise Agreement between Harlem Shake and Franchise India to open 75 units across multiple Indian markets. “India represents an important growth opportunity for Harlem Shake as we begin to expand our presence internationally. We are excited to partner with FranGlobal and Franchise India to introduce our brand to a new market. Harlem Shake has always been about more than burgers and shakes; it is about creating a welcoming experience rooted in culture, community and great food. We look forward to exploring the opportunities India offers and building meaningful connections with consumers and franchise partners, “said Jelena Pasic, Founder and CEO, Harlem Shake The India partnership aligns with Harlem Shake’s broader growth ambitions, leveraging strategic franchise relationships to reach new markets while retaining the brand’s distinctive identity. Through Franchise India and FranGlobal, the brand will explore regional master franchise and regional development opportunities to bring the Harlem Shake experience to the subcontinent of India. “Harlem Shake brings a distinctive New York dining concept to India, combining a recognizable American menu with a strong brand identity and an experience built around community and culture. Through FranGlobal’s international franchising expertise and Franchise India’s understanding of the Indian market, we aim to connect the brand with suitable franchise partners and support its expansion across key Indian territories.” said Mr. Gaurav Marya, Chairman, Franchise India Brands Limited. Harlem Shake is exploring franchise-led expansion opportunities in India through regional master franchise and area-development models. Prospective franchise partners and investors interested in exploring opportunities to bring the brand to their respective markets can connect with Franchise India and FranGlobal for further information on partnership and development opportunities. articles.title: Bread Zeppelin Announces $2 Discount on Chicken Caesar Zeppelin Combo
articles.titleKo: Bread Zeppelin Announces $2 Discount on Chicken Caesar Zeppelin Combo
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . While other sandwich chains are introducing scaled-down options to reach a lower price, Bread Zeppelin is keeping its Chicken Caesar combo exactly the size guests know and charging less for it. From Oct. 21-28, guests at participating Dallas-Fort Worth locations can get the Chicken Caesar Zeppelin combo for $2 less than the usual $9.99. The promotion follows the Oct. 12 rollout of Jersey Mike’s $7.99 Mini Bundle , which features a smaller cold sub and a bag of chips. Bread Zeppelin is matching that price and upping the protein — its Caesar packs 41 grams, roughly 128% more than the 18-gram minimum Jersey Mike’s reports for those sandwiches. “I’m a Jersey Mike’s fan. I’ve got the rewards account to prove it,” said co-founder Troy Charhon. “But I’ll put our deal up against theirs any day. We know many of our neighbors are being more mindful of how they spend their hard-earned money. We want to give them something they can feel good about choosing, without having to compromise on quality or value.” The build features their full-sized toasted baguette, cored out and loaded with romaine, Parmesan, Caesar dressing and chicken marinated and grilled in-house, never frozen — also available as a salad bowl. Even the croutons have a backstory. They’re housemade from the bread cores pulled during prep, so nothing goes to waste. “When we sat down to put this offer together, making the Zeppelin smaller never even came up,” said co-founder Andrew Schoellkopf. “Same delicious baguette, same grilled chicken, same 41 grams of protein. We’d rather just charge less for it and let our guests taste for themselves what all the hype is about.” For more information or to view the menu, visit breadzeppelin.com or follow @breadzeppelin on social media. *While supplies last. Additional restrictions may apply. Available for dine-in, take-out and in app purchases only, no third party orders accepted. The post Bread Zeppelin Announces $2 Discount on Chicken Caesar Zeppelin Combo appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: KNEAD Hospitality + Design Names Juan Pablo Loza Culinary Director of Mi Vida
articles.titleKo: KNEAD Hospitality + Design Names Juan Pablo Loza Culinary Director of Mi Vida
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . KNEAD Hospitality + Design has announced that Chef Juan Pablo Loza has joined Mi Vida as Culinary Director. This is the first menu change of its kind for both KNEAD and Mi Vida since opening in 2018 as the group continues its ongoing market expansion with locations across Washington, D.C., Philadelphia, and Virginia Beach. The exciting new chapter is a culmination of seven years of a professional relationship and friendship with KNEAD Hospitality + Design co-principals, Jason Berry and Michael Reginbogin, who first connected with Loza during his tenure at Rosewood Mayakoba. “We’ve known Chef Juan Pablo for many years and have always admired his approach to cooking and hospitality,” said Berry. “We’ve had the opportunity to watch his career evolve since we first met him at Rosewood Mayakoba, so having him lead the next chapter of Mi Vida’s culinary direction feels like a very natural fit.” Loza grew up in Mexico City’s Xochimilco neighborhood, spending afternoons at the local market with his mother and grandmother cleaning beans and prepping tomatillos. He began training at 16 under French chef Olivier Lombard, followed by four years in the high-pressure kitchen of Mexico City’s Lasser. He went on to win the Guillermo Ríos Young Mexican Chef Competition, a national competition hosted by Ambrosia Centro Culinario and judged by chefs including Enrique Olvera and Ricardo Muñoz Zurita. After culinary positions at Le Cirque, Ciboulette and L’Olivier, Loza built an international hospitality career with Rosewood Hotels & Resorts, Belmond and Auberge Resorts Collection across Mexico, the Caribbean and South America. He spent eight years as Executive Chef and Director of Culinary Operations at Rosewood Mayakoba, overseeing six restaurants and bars—including Zapote Bar, ranked No. 11 on North America’s 50 Best Bars in 2023 and 2024—and transforming a beach food truck he launched into the $8 million Aqui Me Quedo beach club. Most recently, he served as Director of Culinary Experiences at Chileno Bay Resort & Residences before opening Señora Cocina, Casa & Cantina in San José del Cabo in March 2025. His extensive experience across international luxury resort markets gives him a unique perspective on bridging American diners’ tastes with authentic, regional Mexican flavors and ingredients. Loza will bring what he calls his own version of Mexico to the Mi Vida menu – lighter, brighter cooking built on vegetables, acidity, and technique. His approach challenges misconceptions that Mexican cooking is “heavy” by highlighting its fresh, vibrant nature. He’s rebalancing the menu’s traditional weight, turning some of Mi Vida’s richer dishes into starters while building new main courses designed to feel lighter without sacrificing flavor: a chile-rubbed salmon over avocado-citrus purée with a cucumber and preserved lemon salad; ribs reimagined through the lens of tacos al pastor, finished with charred pineapple and cured onion; a crispy pork shank recast as carnitas alongside a bright, citrus-lifted salsa verde; and a banana leaf-wrapped barbacoa short rib served with a chilled, chickpea salad for contrast. A guacamole built with grasshoppers and chorizo, “Guacamole Oaxaca,” reflects his belief that trying something unfamiliar is part of what makes dining out worth it. Mi Vida, Spanish for “my life,” is a fitting name for what Loza calls deeply personal cooking. By merging his culinary vision with KNEAD’s signature design, Loza is looking forward to being a part of DC’s thriving culinary scene. “Cooking has always been a deeply personal expression of who I am, where I come from, and the experiences that have shaped me,” said Loza. “I’m excited to bring my perspective to Mi Vida, while honoring the cuisine I grew up eating. To celebrate the occasion, doors will open at 10 a.m., and the first 50 guests in line will receive an Original ChopShop tote bag with the purchase of any breakfast entrée, bowl, salad or sandwich. Following opening day, Original ChopShop Peoria will be open 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Sunday. To learn more about the feel good brand and explore its extensive menu offerings, visit OriginalChopShop.com. articles.title: Just Salad Announces New Clutch Wrap Created by NBA Star Jalen Brunson
articles.titleKo: Just Salad Announces New Clutch Wrap Created by NBA Star Jalen Brunson
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The new wrap marks the latest step in a partnership designed from the beginning to go beyond a traditional athlete endorsement. Just Salad, the fast-casual restaurant chain committed to making everyday health and sustainability possible, brings The Clutch Wrap to its menu, a limited-time offering created by Jalen Brunson, point guard for the New York Knicks, 2026 NBA Champion and Finals MVP, and Just Salad partner and equity owner. Launching as the NBA season tips off and available at all Just Salad locations through December 31, The Clutch Wrap brings the partnership directly to the menu for the first time, giving guests and fans a new way to experience what Brunson and the New York-born brand are literally building together. The Clutch Wrap layers baby spinach and shredded cabbage with oven roasted chicken, roasted corn, hot honey goat cheese and spicy harissa pita, finished with Just Salad’s homemade Chipotle Vinaigrette. The combination delivers sweet heat, crunch and bold flavor in every bite, featuring 48 grams of protein and 36 grams of fiber. “I wanted this to be something I’d actually order with a lot of flavor, plenty of protein and just the right amount of heat, so we got to work until we got it just right,” said Jalen Brunson, 2026 NBA Champion, NBA Finals MVP and Captain of the New York Knicks . “It’s unreal to now have something on the menu that fans can go in and try for themselves, but starting the season with The Clutch Wrap felt like the right move.” The new wrap marks the latest step in a partnership designed from the beginning to go beyond a traditional athlete endorsement. Brunson joined Just Salad as a partner and equity owner in June before debuting their first creative campaign , “ New York Always Knew ,” built around the fans who believed in both Brunson and the brand long before everyone else caught on. “From day one, this partnership was never about simply putting Jalen’s name on something,” said Nick Kenner, Founder and CEO of Just Salad . “When we announced the partnership, we said Jalen’s impact would become part of the brand in ways our guests would start to see over time. The Clutch Wrap is another step in bringing that to life, and it’s time for guests across all of our locations to taste it for themselves.” The Clutch Wrap continues a relationship centered on shared values, authenticity and building together, as Brunson closely worked alongside Just Salad’s culinary team to craft it. Brunson is expected to continue engaging with Just Salad’s leadership and beyond, visiting restaurants, connecting with guests and continuing to bring his perspective into the business over time. The wrap launch will also be supported by a new connected TV (CTV) spot that puts Brunson’s reputation for coming through in clutch moments front and center. Building on September’s documentary-style ‘New York Always Knew’ campaign, the new creative focuses on the clutch performances that have defined his career and now his first signature Just Salad menu item. The spot will run across select CTV channels as well as out-of-home advertising across Just Salad markets. At Just Salad, health and sustainability are built into every meal, serving approachable, flavor-packed meals. This means homemade dressings, prepped-daily produce, chef-designed recipes and fresh, flavorful ingredients. A leader in sustainable dining for two decades, Just Salad is best known for its reusable bowl program , which rewards guests with a free topping for every reuse, proving that small choices can add up to meaningful impact. Enjoy The Clutch Wrap through December 31 in-restaurant, via mobile app or online at Order.JustSalad.com. articles.title: Olo’s New App Could Change How Restaurants Compete for Digital Orders
articles.titleKo: Olo’s New App Could Change How Restaurants Compete for Digital Orders
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Olo app launches on Tuesday. More than two decades after Noah Glass first envisioned a digital network connecting restaurants and their customers, the Olo founder and CEO is preparing to bring that idea directly to consumers. On Tuesday, Olo will launch its namesake mobile app, giving customers a single destination to order pickup and delivery from restaurants across its network. The platform introduces what Glass calls “second-party” ordering, a model that combines the convenience of third-party marketplaces with the economics and customer relationships associated with restaurants’ direct ordering channels. The proposition is straightforward. Customers can browse multiple brands without paying inflated menu prices, and operators receive the full profit from each order without marketplace commissions. Olo, meanwhile, collects a 5 percent fee from consumers. The launch represents a significant expansion of Olo’s business, taking a company known primarily as a behind-the-scenes technology provider into a consumer-facing market dominated by DoorDash and Uber Eats. Glass says the concept dates to an executive summary he wrote in December 2003, years before Olo became an established restaurant technology provider. “To say that this is like a nearly 23-year dream come true this launch Tuesday is not hyperbole,” Glass says. Olo’s acquisition by private equity firm Thoma Bravo helped accelerate the initiative. Glass says the shift from a publicly traded software provider to a privately owned company created greater flexibility to pursue a network business model. His conviction was significant enough that he and his family reinvested 75 percent of their transaction proceeds into Olo. The immediate opportunity lies in addressing longstanding friction in restaurant digital ordering. Individual restaurant apps can be expensive to acquire customers for and difficult to sustain engagement with. Third-party marketplaces offer considerable consumer reach, but restaurants sacrifice margins through commissions, advertising expenses, and limited access to customer information. Olo believes there is an underserved audience between dedicated restaurantttt loyalists and consumers committed to subscription programs such as DashPass and Uber One. “There’s a big group in the middle, I would argue, and probably the majority of the overall population that wants the convenience of being able to order from many different brands in one place,” Glass says. Glass doesn’t view the app primarily as a vehicle to shift existing transactions away from restaurant-owned channels. He expects the lower cost of ordering to encourage additional occasions among consumers who have become discouraged by delivery prices. The potential savings are a significant component of Olo’s consumer pitch. Glass says menu markups on traditional marketplaces frequently range from 15 to 30 percent, adding costs that customers may mistakenly attribute to restaurants. He points to an $85 delivery order he recently placed through the Olo app that cost $19.34 less than the equivalent marketplace transaction, even after Olo’s 5 percent fee. The platform will disclose that fee during checkout and inform customers that ordering directly from a restaurant is the least expensive option. Delivery fees and tips still apply when customers choose delivery, but Olo avoids the additional menu markups that can make marketplace orders considerably more expensive. Another advantage is that Olo isn’t starting its consumer network from scratch. The company has spent several years building Olo Accounts, a shared login system introduced in 2022 that allows customers to authenticate across participating restaurant brands using an email address or mobile number. articles.title: Carlos Boozer Takes on Role of Chief Growth Officer at Impeccable
articles.titleKo: Carlos Boozer Takes on Role of Chief Growth Officer at Impeccable
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Impeccable announced that co-founder Carlos Boozer has taken on the full-time role of chief growth officer, expanding his involvement with the vertically integrated real estate and restaurant platform as it continues to grow throughout the Southeast. In his new role, Boozer will work across Impeccable Capital’s diverse portfolio, including Impeccable Development and Impeccable Restaurant Group, to strengthen the companies’ public presence, build strategic relationships and identify new business opportunities. He will also participate in executive planning and work directly with leaders across Impeccable’s investment, development and restaurant businesses. “Carlos has been an integral part of Impeccable from the beginning,” said Rob Tanner, founder and CEO of Impeccable. “He has an extraordinary ability to connect with people and see opportunity across industries. We want that perspective involved as we grow our existing businesses and explore what comes next.” “I helped build Impeccable because I believed in what we could create together,” Boozer said. “I’m excited to take a bigger role in the day-to-day business, spending time with our teams, showing up in the communities we serve and bringing the right people together to help us grow.” As chief growth officer, Boozer will help drive Impeccable’s growth by using his visibility, credibility and relationships to open doors to investors, strategic partners and new business opportunities. Working closely with CEO Rob Tanner and the company’s leadership team, he will build key relationships, make qualified introductions and evaluate potential new lines of business. Boozer will represent Impeccable at conferences, speaking engagements, media appearances, investor meetings and company events, including restaurant openings. He will also visit restaurants and development projects, strengthen connections with employees, franchise brands and community leaders, and participate in executive planning to help turn promising opportunities into long-term growth. A two-time NBA All-Star and Olympic gold medalist, Boozer played 13 seasons in the NBA for the Cleveland Cavaliers, Utah Jazz, Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Lakers. He represented the United States at the 2004 and 2008 Olympic Games, winning bronze in Athens and gold in Beijing. The 2008 U.S. Olympic men’s basketball team, known as the “Redeem Team,” was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame as part of its class of 2025. Since retiring from professional basketball, Boozer has focused on entrepreneurship, franchising and commercial real estate. As a co-founder and investor in Impeccable Capital, Impeccable Development and Impeccable Restaurant Group, he also serves on Impeccable Development’s board of directors and real estate committee. Boozer’s expanded role comes as Impeccable continues to scale its real estate development and restaurant operations throughout the Southeast. Impeccable Development has more than 25 active projects, with approximately 2 million square feet developed or under development. The company specializes in ground-up retail, restaurant and select mixed-use developments, working with national and regional brands throughout its portfolio. Boozer’s transition into a full-time role reflects Impeccable’s plans to expand its development and restaurant businesses, strengthen its investment platform and explore new lines of business. Bringing him into the company’s day-to-day leadership allows him to apply his relationships, visibility and credibility more directly to those priorities. As chief growth officer, he will help attract investors, build strategic partnerships and identify opportunities that support Impeccable’s next phase of growth. Looking ahead, 2027 and 2028 are shaping up to be an exciting next chapter, with major acquisitions, new brands and strategic partnership
