articles.title: What the Meritage Chapter 11 Teaches Restaurant Franchisees
articles.titleKo: What the Meritage Chapter 11 Teaches Restaurant Franchisees
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Meritage shows that a single day can decide whether a debtor has hundreds of restaurants to reorganize or none at all. One day after Wendy’s cut it loose, the operator of 314 Wendy’s-franchised restaurants filed for bankruptcy to keep its franchises alive. The case tests a question many distressed franchisees face: Can bankruptcy save a franchise the franchisor says is already gone? Timing and venue are critical. Quality Is Our Recipe, LLC (“QIOR”), a Wendy’s subsidiary, notified Meritage Hospitality Group on Sept. 16, 2026, that all its franchise agreements were terminated “effective immediately.” Meritage, which operates 314 franchised restaurants in 15 states, filed chapter 11 the next day in the Western District of Michigan to stay termination. In re Meritage Hospitality Group Inc. , No. 26-02947 (Bankr. W.D. Mich.). QIOR claims roughly $146.9 million, including $119.5 million in “continuous operations fees.” The Adversary Proceeding On October 1, 2026, the debtors sued QIOR and Wendy’s seeking declaratory relief that the termination was ineffective, the franchise agreements are estate property and the automatic stay bars enforcement. The dispute traces to an October 2025 payment-default notice and three forbearance letters, the last expiring August 18, 2026. QIOR’s emailed termination notice demanded more than $146 million by Oct. 16, 2026, and tendered a short-term license agreement (“STLA”) through year-end. The debtors allege the termination failed because the agreements required physical (not email) notice; QIOR did not give lenders the required notice and cure opportunity under the consents to collateral assignment; cure periods restarted upon forbearance expiration; and the STLA and QIOR’s reserved purchase option presupposed a continuing relationship. Can Chapter 11 Resurrect a Terminated Franchise Agreement? The answer turns on timing. A franchise agreement not fully terminated at filing becomes estate property under 11 U.S.C. § 541, and the automatic stay (§ 362(a)) bars termination without stay relief. See In re Welcome Group 2, LLC , 660 B.R. 874, 879 (Bankr. S.D. Ohio 2024); In re Mirant Corp. , 440 F.3d 238, 252–53 (5th Cir. 2006). Conversely, contracts that have expired or were validly terminated prior to bankruptcy leave the debtor “with nothing to assume or reject.” In re P.I.N.E., Inc. , 52 B.R. 463, 465 (Bankr. W.D. Mich. 1985). QIOR and Wendy’s respond that the agreements “have been terminated” and are not estate property. Meritage argues that even a valid termination leaves residual interests, including the right to seek reinstatement. Meritage’s fight turns on whether the Sept. 16 notice completed the job or merely started a process interrupted by the stay. The notice reserved QIOR’s options to buy equipment and take over leases, obligations Meritage calls “diametrically inconsistent” with a completed termination. The default notice set state-specific cure periods of 90, 60 and 30 days, later deferred by forbearance, inviting arguments that fresh notice was required. The interim license offer arguably belies a clean break. And the lender-notice argument may prove decisive; QIOR admits the consent language but pleads compliance. Notably, a bare right to terminate may not itself establish “cause” for stay relief under § 362(d)(1). See Mirant , 440 F.3d at 253. Meritage’s Restructuring Strategy and Operations Meritage operates as a debtor in possession, with a strategy of closing or selling underperforming stores, resolving the QIOR dispute, potential market sales and a recapitalization. Its chief restructuring officer calls Wendy’s system access “indispensable to any viable restructuring.” The interim cash collateral order requires closing at least 30 EBITDA-negative stores by Oct. 16; termination of the Wendy’s agreements, or a finding that they were terminated, is a cash collateral

articles.title: New York–Style Pizzeria Barsella to Open Near SMU’s Campus
articles.titleKo: New York–Style Pizzeria Barsella to Open Near SMU’s Campus
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A new locally-owned restaurant and bar is coming to SMU Boulevard this winter. Barsella, an Italian-American restaurant, New York-style pizzeria and cocktail bar, will open at 5600 SMU Blvd., Suite 120 in Dallas for dinner and late night, with slices from a walk-up window during the day. Barsella is the first hospitality concept from Dallas native Oliver Steinberg. Barsella is meant to work for more than one kind of night. Guests can settle in for dinner and a bottle of wine, meet friends for happy hour, grab a New York-style slice from the window, enjoy spritzes on the patio or end the evening with drinks and late-night bites. “Barsella was designed in hopes of becoming a neighborhood institution, elevated enough for a great dinner or date night, approachable enough to become your regular spot, and lively enough to be where you want to end the night,” says Dallas resident and creator of the concept, Oliver Steinberg. “We wanted to create a place where families, couples, friends and neighbors all feel equally at home, whatever brings them in that night,” he adds. From the dining room to the slice window, each space has its own identity and energy, all served by the same kitchen and consistent approach to food and hospitality. At its core, the new restaurant offers a thoughtful take on Italian-American dining. “The menu is intentionally filled with dishes people know, love and want to order such as rigatoni alla vodka, ravioli and lasagna, yet executed at a high level,” expresses Steinberg. Many dishes take inspiration from iconic New York pizzerias and restaurants the culinary team visited while developing the menu. The goal is food that is craveable and memorable without ever feeling overly complicated or intimidating, paired with an extensive spritz and craft cocktail program and a thoughtfully developed wine list. New York-style pizza isn’t an accessory to the bar or dining room; it is one of the foundations of the concept. Inside, a seven-seat pizza bar offers a more casual way to experience the restaurant, sharing the slice window’s menu along with offerings beyond pizza. Walking up to the slice window is meant to feel like stepping beneath the marquee of a Broadway theater, with bright, theatrical signage recognizable from down the street. The window serves individual slices from a mix of staple pies and rotating specials. The patio, envisioned as a bit of an Italian escape with a pergola and lemon-vine plantings overhead, is a natural place to enjoy one, and large sliding windows connect it to the interior bar. As dinner fades into night, Barsella becomes a late-night spritz and cocktail bar. Live music fills the room most Thursday through Saturday nights, and a dedicated menu of light bites, featuring dishes guests won’t find everywhere else, is served until 2 a.m. An intimate private dining room of approximately 16 seats can also host private dinners, celebrations and events, carrying the same green tones, tile and millwork throughout. Liz Johnson of Wallace Johnson Studio is leading the interior design, drawing on classic Italian-American concepts, New York cafés and European aperitivo culture for a space that feels polished, bright and colorful rather than dark and rustic. Hexagonal mosaic floors, olive-green millwork, green tile and red pleated booths set the tone inside the approximately 3,100-square-foot space which will seat 80 in the main dining room. Barsella is slated to open this winter at 5600 SMU Blvd., Suite 120, Dallas, Texas. Additional details on the menu and opening date will be announced closer to opening. articles.title: Hangry Joe’s New CEO Wants to Build a Better Franchise System, Not Just a Bigger One
articles.titleKo: Hangry Joe’s New CEO Wants to Build a Better Franchise System, Not Just a Bigger One
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Brandon Wihelm was named Hangry Joe's CEO in early October. Brandon Wilhelm wasn’t necessarily looking to take on another major role in the restaurant industry. After spending nearly two decades developing Subway franchise territory across the Midwest, he was considering opportunities outside the business. Then he discovered Hangry Joe’s. Wilhelm traveled to Virginia to explore the emerging hot chicken concept, arriving a day early to secretly visit several restaurants before meeting with the corporate team. He came away impressed with the food, but also saw opportunities to improve the young franchise’s marketing, real estate strategy, and operational infrastructure. That combination eventually led him to become a multi-unit franchisee, equity investor, board member, and, as of October 6, CEO of the growing fast-casual chain. “I went out to Virginia and and tried the food and checked out the brand and it was the best chicken sandwich I ever had,” Wilhelm says. Founded in 2021, Hangry Joe’s has expanded to more than 90 restaurants across over 20 states and international markets, including the United Arab Emirates. Another 20 locations are in the pipeline. But Wilhelm isn’t measuring the company’s future success solely through restaurant count. His immediate priority is creating a more profitable, sustainable franchise system that can support expansion without repeating some of the mistakes that accompanied its early growth. His experience includes overseeing operations strategy for more than 500 Subway restaurants and working with more than 140 franchisees. He also served as president of Hangry Development Texas and acting chief marketing officer of Hangry Joe’s. Those experiences informed a series of proposals he presented to the company’s founders and board over the past year. The discussions eventually resulted in an invitation to implement the plans himself. “I have no real desire to say, ‘OK, we’re going to grow this to a certain level and then we’re going to sell it to private equity.’ That’s never been my goal, and I’ve told those guys from the beginning,” Wilhelm says. Wilhelm’s initial priorities include reducing food costs, improving purchasing efficiency, increasing consumer awareness, and establishing more rigorous development standards. Supply chain improvements represent one of the most immediate opportunities. Historically, individual franchisees have had considerable flexibility in sourcing certain products, creating inconsistencies that can limit the company’s purchasing power. Wilhelm wants greater compliance with approved distribution relationships to negotiate more favorable pricing across the system. The company is also examining freight expenses, including proprietary ingredients that some operators currently purchase by the pallet and ship directly to individual restaurants. Consolidating those purchases through distribution facilities could eliminate unnecessary expenses and make inventory replenishment more efficient. Additional opportunities include renegotiating vendor agreements and examining third-party delivery commission rates. The challenge is lowering expenses without changing the ingredients and preparation methods that distinguish Hangry Joe’s from competitors. “Our product and our process and all that kind of stuff is not going to change,” Wilhelm says. “Our proprietary seasonings, our proprietary marinade, and the quality of chicken that we get in, none of that’s going to change.” The same attention to unit economics is influencing Hangry Joe’s development strategy. articles.title: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.titleKo: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s same-store sales have gained a collective 50 percent over the past three years. So, CMO and EVP George Felix wasn’t dealing in hyperbole when he told investors recently the brand had been “pretty busy.” What Chili’s was up to boils down to a few investment-laden storylines. The company spent $100 million-plus in facilities. It reworked hospitality by pouring back into labor. Chili’s refocused on core execution and menu architecture. But when talking about one of the most-vivid turnarounds in category history, people often start with how loud the brand became. Chili’s in that opening calendar under Felix and CEO Kevin Hochmann—who worked together at Yum! Brands—spent about $32 million in marketing. Three years later, the figure was closer to $132 million. Felix during Brinker’s investor day dove deeper into what’s been the most outward effect of that higher backing: value perception. This chart below, which uses YouGov data, lays out value perception scores among the general population of adults 18–49. Since rerouting, Chili’s result increased by 50 percent, placing it atop the company’s competitive set, widely speaking. However, Felix said, what’s more interesting is the following, which unpacks how value perception turned among customers who saw the brand’s advertising in the past two weeks. Trends were similar. There, too, Chili’s witnessed a sizable increase over the past three years. And again, it topped the competitive field. “But you can see that the increase in value perception is much bigger and the gap between us and competition is much wider,” Felix explained. What that tells Felix, he continued, is Chili’s “Better Than Fast Food” campaign continues to resonate. When customers find the messaging, it makes them think differently about the value Chili’s offers. What gives Chili’s confidence there’s still room to go? “Well,” Felix said, “when you think about ad awareness and the way to think about ad awareness is that is basically asking consumers, ‘have you seen a brand’s advertising in the past two weeks?’” MORE: Chili’s Turnaround Clears Way for New Restaurant Growth How Chili’s Plans to Remain ‘America’s Hottest Restaurant Brand’ For Chili’s, that particular measure hiked roughly 40 percent over the last three years. You’d expect it to, Felix said, when you toss $100 million into the mix. Yet Chili’s, even with such a vivid bump, still trails the largest spenders in its category. “And so that tells me that there are still probably large pieces of the population that have not seen or been exposed to the ‘Better Than Fast Food’ campaign,” Felix said. “And if you look at the last chart, you know that once we do get people to see that, it does change the way that they think about Chili’s.” In plain terms, Chili’s marketing hook has been to reintroduce guests to a brand they might have lapsed on. How they feel about it. What it offers compared to competitors. And then, invest via operations in an experience and environment worth coming back to. That education process, Felix said, remains underway. There’s also the familiar question marketers face—how have holistic metrics translated to sales? Felix pulled up a slide on Chili’s “Five to Drive” categories. Years ago, in 2017, Chili’s slashed 50 menu items and started to refocus on core products. Its offerings had ballooned to 125 items (40 percent cut). That work continued when Hochman arrived, with about 60 percent of the menu getting renovated. Chili’s sliced more than 25 percent of overall items and moved, as Felix said, to what the brand was known for: burgers, crispers, fajitas, margaritas, and now, the Triple Dipper. Meanwhile, Chili’s devised a heavy labor approach where, when 2026 rolled around, the company was investing $160 million more than it did in fiscal 2022. articles.title: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.titleKo: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. The Honey Baked Ham Company today announced Kylie Kelce, podcast host of “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce” and mom of four, as its brand ambassador and launched “Traditions That Bring Us Home,” a new holiday campaign celebrating how family traditions evolve from one generation to the next. The national campaign runs across TV, streaming, digital, social, and radio now through the holiday season. For generations, HoneyBaked has been part of the moments families look forward to year after year. “Traditions That Bring Us Home” celebrates those moments: the traditions we look forward to, the ways each generation makes them its own, and the people who make them feel like home. For Kelce, that idea is personal. HoneyBaked has been on her family’s holiday table for years, from the signature Bone-In Ham that always makes the menu to the Cinnamon Apples her grandmother, Mimi, loved. After Mimi passed, the family kept serving them in her memory. Today, they’re a favorite with Kelce’s own daughters. “HoneyBaked has been part of my family’s holiday traditions for years, so creating this campaign with a brand I genuinely love was really special,” said Kelce. “The Bone-in Ham is always a centerpiece at our house, and there are certain things you have to have around it: the Double Cheddar Mac & Cheese, the Maple Sweet Potato Souffle, the Rolls, and, of course, the Cinnamon Apples. Those were my Mimi’s favorite, so after she passed, we kept serving them for her. Now all four of my girls love them, even though Wyatt was the only one who got to meet her. I love that something as simple as a favorite food can keep a piece of someone, and a family tradition, going.” As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. She shows how a new generation is holding onto the traditions it grew up with while creating new ones that fit how families gather today. “We’re incredibly excited to partner with Kylie as our brand ambassador this holiday season and begin this next chapter for HoneyBaked together. Kylie is a natural fit for HoneyBaked. Her connection to our brand is authentic, and she brings a fresh, relatable perspective on how families host and gather today,” said Maegan Markee, Chief Commercial Officer at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “She represents a generation that’s taking the traditions they grew up with and making them their own, which is exactly the spirit of ‘Traditions That Bring Us Home.’ This holiday also marks the start of a broader marketing transformation for HoneyBaked, one that honors our heritage and celebrates our loyalists while finding new ways to connect with the next generation of HoneyBaked customers.” “The best holiday meals aren’t about spending all day in the kitchen, they’re about getting everyone around the table,” said Chef Tim Ziga, Culinary Director at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “HoneyBaked has always made that part easier. Whether it’s a big holiday dinner or a busy night with the family, we want to give people great food and more time to actually enjoy the moment.” HoneyBaked’s holiday menu includes its signature Honey Baked Ham, smoked for up to 24 hours and individually hand-glazed with its sweet and crunchy glaze, along with premium turkey breasts, heat-and-serve sides and desserts. Guests can plan ahead by ordering now at HoneyBaked.com and scheduling in-store pickup closer to Thanksgiving or the holidays. The full menu is available at participating locations nationwide and through HoneyBaked.com. Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria announced today that its highly anticipated St. Charles restaurant will officially open Tuesday, October 27 at 3050 E. Main St., further expanding the family-owned company’s presence in the Chicagoland area. The restaurant marks Lou Malnati’s 70th location and will employ approximately 100 team members. The 6,200-square-foot space features a full-service dining room and bar, private dining room, carryout, delivery and catering services. “The St. Charles restaurant represents an exciting milestone in our continued Chicagoland growth,” said Julie Younglove-Webb, CEO of Lou Malnati’s. “Since 1971, we’ve been focused on bringing people together over our handmade deep dish, and we look forward to putting down roots in St. Charles, building lasting relationships and becoming a trusted part of the community for years to come.” “We’re thrilled to welcome Lou Malnati’s to Fox Haven Square and see this highly anticipated addition open its doors,” said Pat Greco, president of G Ninety Family Partners. “Lou’s is an iconic Chicago brand, and we believe the restaurant will be a tremendous addition to both the development and the St. Charles community.” Guests can enjoy the full Lou Malnati’s menu, including its legendary Chicago-style deep dish pizza made with its signature flaky buttercrust, Wisconsin mozzarella cheese and vine-ripened tomato sauce, as well as thin crust pizza, gluten-free options, appetizers, salads, pastas and desserts. The St. Charles restaurant will also be the first Lou Malnati’s location to showcase elements of the company’s refreshed brand experience. Updated visual elements, menu design and interior finishes blend the rich history of the Malnati family with a modern, welcoming atmosphere. To create a restaurant that reflects its new hometown, Lou Malnati’s worked with the St. Charles History Museum to incorporate historic photographs and local storytelling throughout the space. The restaurant design also features family photographs, pizza-pan-inspired décor and subtle nods to the Malnati family’s legacy and Chicago roots. As Lou Malnati’s continues to expand throughout the Chicagoland area, the company remains committed to being more than a restaurant in the communities it serves. Through local partnerships, charitable involvement and genuine hospitality, Lou Malnati’s looks forward to supporting local organizations and becoming an active member of the St. Charles community for generations to come. The restaurant is located in the Fox Haven Square development near the northeast corner of Kirk Road and East Main Street. For more information, please visit loumalnatis.com. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy’s is putting a square deal on the table. Starting today, customers can score a Dave’s Single combo meal, featuring a Dave’s Single hamburger, small Hot & Crispy Fries, and a small soft drink for just $7.99 – proving fans don’t have to choose between quality and value at Wendy’s. Wendy’s goes the extra mile for each customer, delivering quality food at a price that feels as good as it tastes. The Dave’s Single is a delicious example of that standard. Named after Wendy’s founder, Dave Thomas, the iconic hamburger is made to order with a quarter pound of 100% Fresh, Never Frozen beef*, American cheese, lettuce, tomato, pickle, ketchup, mustard, mayo and onion on a toasted potato bun. WHEN & WHERE: Starting October 19: For a limited time only, fans can order a Dave’s Single combo meal – including a Dave’s Single, small Hot & Crispy Fries and your choice of a small soft drink for just $7.99 at participating U.S. Wendy’s restaurants.** Available to order: In-restaurant, through the drive-thru or via the Wendy’s app and Wendy’s.com . WHY: Wendy’s knows great taste, quality ingredients and exceptional value should go hand in hand. The $7.99 Dave’s Single Combo shines a spotlight on one of Wendy’s most iconic menu items. With roots dating back to the brand’s original five menu offerings, the Dave’s Single has long reflected Wendy’s commitment to serving fresh, quality food without cutting corners. Whether it’s a quick drive-thru visit or dinner for the family, customers can enjoy the Wendy’s quality they love at a price that delivers outstanding value. *Approximate weight before cooking. Fresh beef available in the contiguous U.S. and Alaska, as well as Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, the UK, and other select international markets. **Limited time only. U.S. price and participation may vary. Not valid with any other offer or discount. No substitutions. Prices may be higher for delivery. articles.title: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.titleKo: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. The Kolache Factory, the Katy-based bakery-café franchise known for its fresh-baked kolaches, is giving customers what they asked for. After a record-breaking limited-time run, the brand’s Birria Kolache has officially earned a permanent spot on the menu at all Kolache Factory locations. The Birria Kolache was inspired by Erin Hargett of Greenville, South Carolina, who submitted the idea as part of Kolache Factory’s annual Create a Kolache Contest. The customer-created flavor was introduced systemwide as the brand’s April 2026 Flavor of the Month and quickly became Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales. During its 30-day limited-time run, the Birria Kolache delivered strong systemwide results, including: 43,523 Birria Kolaches sold across all 60 stores 1.8 times the average Flavor of the Month sales per store per day More than 10,000 Birria Kolaches sold per week on average The results made the Birria Kolache Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales and helped drive the decision to add it to the permanent menu. “The Birria Kolache is exactly what our Create a Kolache Contest is all about,” said Dawn Nielsen, COO of Kolache Factory. “A customer brought us a bold idea and our team brought it to life, and guests responded in a big way. When a limited-time flavor performs like this and customers keep asking for it, we listen.” Priced at $4.98*, the Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. Unlike traditional birria dishes that are often served with consommé on the side for dipping, Kolache Factory bakes the consommé inside the kolache, creating a portable, flavor-packed version of the popular dish. The permanent menu addition reflects Kolache Factory’s approach to menu innovation, blending global flavors with the brand’s Czech-inspired roots while staying close to what customers want. The brand’s annual Create a Kolache Contest, now in its 8 th year, invites fans to submit original flavor ideas, giving customers a direct role in shaping future menu items. Winning submissions usually get a place on the menu as a limited-time offering. This is the first time a submission has been added to the permanent menu. “Kolache Factory has always been built around approachable, craveable flavors that fit into everyday routines,” Nielsen said. “The Birria Kolache brings something bold and unexpected to the menu, while still staying true to what people love about our kolaches.” The Birria Kolache is now available at all Kolache Factory locations. To learn more or find a location, visit www.kolachefactory.com. *Prices may vary in certain states. articles.title: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.titleKo: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies. The international journey of SIGEP Meets the World, the Italian Exhibition Group (IEG) roadshow organised in collaboration with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA), continues. Today, 19 October, the initiative stops in Poland at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw, aiming to strengthen dialogue with the Polish market and create new opportunities for Italian foodservice companies to meet local industry professionals. POLAND: A MARKET OF OPPORTUNITY FOR MADE IN ITALY Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies: coffee, bread and bakery products, pastry products, chocolate, gelato and other food preparations. In 2025, Polish imports of these products reached €8.22 billion, an increase of 26.1% on the previous year. Over the same period, imports from Italy in these same categories rose to €865.3 million, recording growth of 25.3%. Polish imports of machinery and equipment for food preparation and production also showed a positive trend, pointing to further opportunities for Italian companies specialising in technologies for the sector. WARSAW: THE ROAD TO SIGEP WORLD 2027 The event on 19 October, hosted at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw and aimed at industry professionals, will provide an opportunity to present SIGEP World 2027, highlighting its main new features, business opportunities and services for international operators. The programme will also feature a roundtable discussion on the outlook and opportunities for foodservice in the Polish market. Moderated by Natalia Aurora Urbanek, editor-in-chief of the trade magazine Mistrz Branży, the discussion will bring together entrepreneurs and experts from the gelato, pastry and Ho.Re.Ca. sectors to explore consumer trends, market developments and the needs of local operators. The meeting will conclude with a networking session, accompanied by a live demonstration and gelato tasting led by Polish master gelato maker Tomasz Szypuła. The Polish stop is therefore offering an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of market dynamics, engage with local operators and showcase the expertise of Italian companies. The event is part of the journey towards SIGEP World 2027 – The World Expo for Foodservice Excellence, scheduled to take place at Rimini Expo Centre from 23 to 27 January 2027. The 48th edition of the exhibition will bring together the pizza, coffee, bread, pastry, chocolate and gelato supply chains, along with the technologies and services driving the sector’s evolution. “Italian gastronomy tells the story of our regions, artisanal know-how and a culture of hospitality that is part of our identity,” says Luca Franchetti Pardo, Italian Ambassador to Poland. “Gelato is one of the most familiar expressions of this heritage, which continues to evolve through creativity and a commitment to quality. We are delighted to welcome SIGEP Meets the World to the Embassy and to share this tradition with Polish professionals, whose talent and experience enrich today’s gathering. A shared passion such as this also deepens mutual understanding and strengthens the economic ties and bonds of friendship between Italy and Poland.” “The Polish market is showing growing interest in Italian foodservice products and solutions, with positive import trends confirming opportunities for our companies, including in professional technologies and equipment,” says Roberto Cafiero, Director of the Italian Trade Agency’s Warsaw Office. “The Warsaw event forms part of the broader collaboration between the Italian Trade Agency and Italian Exhibition Group, aimed at strengthening the international reach of Italian trade fairs and enhancing their role as global platforms for

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . OHG Brands, parent company of Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express , has officially opened a new co-branded location in Eagle Pass, TX. Located at 3777 El Indio Hwy., the new restaurant brings Fatburger’s hand-pressed burgers, fries and hand-scooped milkshakes alongside Buffalo Express’ craveable chicken wings to the community, complete with a convenient drive-thru designed for guests to grab their favorites on the go. Recognized as a Hollywood-favorite, Fatburger has built a reputation for its wide menu variety, including grilled-to-perfection and cooked-to-order burgers, which can be customized with signature toppings including bacon, eggs, chili and onion rings. From Buffalo’s Express, guests can dig into bone-in and boneless chicken wings tossed in a variety of mouthwatering sauces. “Our new Eagle Pass drive-thru location provides added convenience and flexibility, allowing us to serve both local residents and the many travelers passing through Eagle Pass,” said Jake Berchtold, COO of OHG Brands’ Fast Casual Division. “We’re excited to open our doors and deliver the quality, flavor and hospitality our fans know and love.” “We’re incredibly excited to open our doors and welcome the Eagle Pass community,” said the De Los Santos family, franchise owners of the Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express Eagle Pass location. “We look forward to creating a place where families and friends can come together and enjoy the Fatburger experience.” The new Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express is located at 3777 El Indio Hwy. in Eagle Pass, TX, and is open Sunday through Thursday from 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m., and Friday through Saturday from 11 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. For more information on Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express, visit www.fatburger.com. articles.title: Le Colonial Delray Beach Expands Group Dining With New Menus and Experiences
articles.titleKo: Le Colonial Delray Beach Expands Group Dining With New Menus and Experiences
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Le Colonial Delray Beach, the acclaimed French-Vietnamese restaurant inspired by the elegance of 1920s Saigon, has unveiled new private dining and catering menus, expanding its offerings for intimate dinners, corporate gatherings, holiday parties and other special events, just in time for the holidays. Private dining options include The Parrot Room, an intimate private dining room for up to 12 guests; The Lounge, accommodating up to 40 seated or 80 standing with its own private bar; the lush, covered Outdoor Patio, hosting up to 70 guests; or the Main Dining Room, which seats 80 and is available for exclusive buyouts upon request. Private events feature Le Colonial’s signature family-style dining experience, with customizable three-course and four-course menus, as well as the Le Colonial 1993 tasting experience. Lunch packages begin at $65 per guest, while dinner packages start at $100 per guest. Dietary accommodations, including halal offerings with advance notice, are also available. For gatherings beyond the restaurant, Le Colonial has also introduced new catering menus for groups of 10 to 45 guests. The catering program features customizable à la carte selections and family-style packages showcasing favorites such as Vietnamese rolls, Heritage Pork Ribs, Chicken Curry, Roasted Salmon, Shaking Beef and Signature Fried Rice. Signature packages, including The Le Colonial Table and the Golden Saigon Package, offer curated selections of appetizers, entrées, sides and desserts for effortless entertaining. Whether hosting an executive dinner, milestone celebration, wedding event, holiday party or catered gathering, Le Colonial Delray Beach pairs timeless ambiance, exceptional cuisine and gracious hospitality to create memorable experiences both in the restaurant and beyond. articles.title: Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe
articles.titleKo: Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Captain D’s, the leading fast-casual seafood franchise in the United States, is building momentum for international growth as interest from prospective franchise partners expands across Europe. Following a successful international development trip earlier this year, Senior Vice President of International Operations and Development Hair Parra will return to Europe in October to meet with prospective franchisees and explore opportunities in additional markets. The trip is tentatively planned for the second week of October and is expected to include Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom, with additional markets potentially added. Interest in Italy has been particularly active, with Captain D’s currently in conversations with prospective partners. The company is also exploring opportunities in Spain, including Madrid and Valencia, while Poland and France remain markets of interest. “Every time we travel internationally, we come home with more conversations and more new relationships,” said Parra. “It’s exciting to get meaningful interest from experienced operators who recognize the opportunity in bringing a proven American seafood brand to their markets.” The international momentum comes as Captain D’s enters a new phase of U.S. growth, highlighted by the September unveiling of its new restaurant design in San Antonio, Texas. The location is the first U.S. showcase for a refreshed experience, featuring a contemporary design and more inviting guest environment while maintaining the brand’s familiar identity. Captain D’s plans to introduce the new design in additional U.S. markets, including Florida, Ohio and Oklahoma, while continuing to pursue qualified international partners. “Our growth story is bigger than opening individual restaurants,” said Brad Reed, Chief Development Officer for Captain D’s. “We’re evolving the Captain D’s experience while staying true to what has made the brand successful for more than five decades. That combination is creating interest from operators who want to be part of the next chapter of Captain D’s, both here in the U.S. and internationally.” Captain D’s is seeking experienced restaurant operators, multi-unit franchisees and master franchise partners interested in developing multiple locations internationally. Prospective partners can contact franchising@captainds.com. The post Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: TGI Fridays Crowns World’s Best Bartender Amid Global Comeback
articles.titleKo: TGI Fridays Crowns World’s Best Bartender Amid Global Comeback
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . TGI Fridays, where the world goes to celebrate, brought together eight of the brand’s best bartenders from across the world to compete in the 29 th World Bartender Championship (WBC), a flagship event at its Global Business Conference in Orlando. During a week focused on global brand momentum, the friendly competition between TGI Fridays’ most skilled bartenders really brought the spirit of the brand to life. Bartenders representing Japan, Greece, the UK, USA, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, and the Philippines showcased their bottle-spinning skills, with the crown going to Roniel Lopez from TGI Fridays, Manila. The contestants were judged by an expert panel on a combination of technical precision, brand knowledge, speed, and showmanship, while displaying the freestyle flair, personality, and lively personality that is synonymous with TGI Fridays. “It was a privilege to enjoy the skills and technical craft shown by the finalists, and I couldn’t be prouder of the eight experts who competed. Congratulations to Roniel on an impressive performance, and we hope visitors to our Manila restaurant enjoy seeing him in action” said Ray Blanchette, CEO, TGI Fridays. “The Global Business Conference was the perfect setting to bring the WBC back and give attendees an opportunity to show their support for colleagues and enjoy such an integral part of Fridays history.” TGI Fridays Global Business Conference saw brand leaders, franchisees and team members from more than 40 countries come together to discuss the global momentum of Fridays “1-2-3 Strategic Vision,” a growth plan to surpass 1,000 units and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Under the theme “Fridays United,” the conference celebrated the company’s ongoing domestic and international resurgence. Fridays leaders took part in educational sessions and an interactive peer-driven Q&A panel on how regions tailor local strategies while staying true to global brand standards. They also heard from the teams behind several notable 2026 milestones, including the company’s first U.S. development agreement in more than a decade and entry into new territories that includes Pakistan, the Balkans, and Sub-Saharan Africa. “Working in the hospitality industry opens a world of opportunities, and TGI Fridays believes it is the responsibility of every team member to demonstrate their commitment to improving how we show hospitality to our guests,” said Phil Broad, Global President, TGI Fridays International. “Fridays United is an ethos that reflects the culture and mindset we are embracing globally across the brand, centered on collaboration, continuous improvement, and a commitment to making TGI Fridays our guests’ favorite choice. That spirit was on full display at our Global Business Conference that saw our leaders come together to share ideas, learn, and celebrate the future of the brand.” To learn more about TGI Fridays franchise opportunities, please visit www. tgifridays.com/franchise/. articles.title: Baccarat Hotel New York Names New Executive Chef and Head Sommelier
articles.titleKo: Baccarat Hotel New York Names New Executive Chef and Head Sommelier
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Baccarat Hotel New York , the Forbes Five Star AAA and Five Diamond hotel, announces the appointment of two food and beverage team leaders at the award-winning property. Chef Isaac Olivo has been named the Executive Chef, and In this role, he will collaborate with Chef Gabriel Kreuther, the hotel’s Two Michelin-starred Culinary Director in overseeing all food and beverage operations. This includes the Grand Salon, The Bar and Le Jardin, private events, and in-room dining. Beata Parzych is the new Head Sommelier, where she will oversee the entire wine program at the flagship property which includes the Grand Salon, The Bar, in-room dining, private bar service, and catered events. Chef Olivo brings nearly 20 years of culinary experience to this new position, having worked at world-renowned kitchens around the country and under acclaimed chefs. His previous work experience includes Executive Chef roles at two esteemed Relais & Châteaux establishments; Cuvee Restaurant at The Chatham Inn in Chatham, MA, and the Mayflower Inn & Spa in Washington, CT. Chef Olivo also held culinary leadership positions at Amorette Restaurant in Lancaster, PA, and Restaurant Clement in The Peninsula, New York. He began his career as a Sous Chef at Bourbon Steak by Michael Mina in Miami, FL, and his work experience includes tenure at SHO by Sean Hergatt in NYC, The Villa by Barton G in Miami Beach, and Jean Georges in NYC. A New York City native of Dominican heritage, Chef Olivo earned a Culinary Arts Diploma from Le Cordon Bleu and brings passion, creativity, and refined technique to the kitchen. Inspired by his father and grandmother, he discovered his love for cooking at an early age. Known for his seasonal, sustainable approach, Chef Olivo blends French technique with contemporary American flavors while honoring craftsmanship, culture and mentorship. He has also represented Relais & Châteaux at international events such as World Oceans Day, advocating for sustainability and ocean conservation. “I am thrilled to be part of something shaped by a pedigree rooted in centuries of excellence, craftsmanship, and an appreciation for the art of living well, and my goal is to bring this spirit to the table,” says Chef Olivo. “Baccarat Hotel New York is a celebration of joie de vivre which honors tradition while also embracing the inventiveness of today’s modern culinary landscape and for me it is all about creating cuisine that feels both timeless and contemporary at this sparkling property,” he adds. With nearly 20 years of experience in fine dining and luxury hospitality, Beata’s brings her expertise in wine, exceptional service, and the art of creating memorable guest experiences to her new role. Prior to joining the hotel, she worked at a variety of premier Michelin-starred establishments in New York City, including Le Bernardin, and Le Cirque and Circo Restaurants. Beata also held beverage leadership and sommelier positions at BLT Restaurant Group, STK Saint Urban, Rhubard Hospitality Collection, STK, and Zuma, all in the city. “In my new role I am excited to bring together my passion for continually evolving within the world of wine and hospitality, with a thoughtful, guest-focused approach to leadership, “ says Beata. “My focus is on maintaining high standards while building a collaborative team culture, while ensuring that knowledge, consistency, and genuine hospitality come together in every guest interaction,” she adds. With six locations now serving the Dallas area, including a new location that opened last week at Preston and Belt Line (14999 Preston Rd., Ste 226, Dallas 75254), Snarf’s is building a growing following among North Texas diners looking for a sandwich experience that stands apart from the ordinary. articles.title: Vietnamese Sandwich Concept Bun Mee Opens in New York City
articles.titleKo: Vietnamese Sandwich Concept Bun Mee Opens in New York City
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bun Mee, the gourmet Vietnamese sandwich eatery founded in 2011 by Denise Tran and recognized by Bloomberg and Forbes, is now open in New York City (its first market outside of San Francisco) as the brand celebrates 15 years in business. The first store is located in the Flatiron neighborhood at 115 E 23rd St and officially opened on October 8, 2026. The menu features creative takes on the bánh mì sandwich , alongside salads and bowls , shareable sides , and specialty beverages. Signature items include the Classic Combo (grilled lemongrass pork, pate de campagne, mortadella, shaved onion, pickled carrot and daikon, jalapeńos, cucumber, herb mix, and garlic house mayo on a toasted baguette), a Ribeye Steak Dip (a pho-inspired juicy steak ribeye, bean sprouts, herb mix, garlic house mayo on a toasted baguette and served with pho broth), Salt & Pepper Garlic Fries tossed with chopped red onions and jalapeńos and drinks such as the Vietnamese Cream Cloud made with Vietnamese coffee, and topped with rich soft whip and 5-spice powder. The baguettes are specially baked fresh daily by a local baker adhering to Bun Mee’s specifications. All three locations will be owned and operated by the McClave family: John McClave, a real estate professional; his wife, Nam; their son, Egan; and Nam’s brother, Huy. “We spent a lot of time researching different franchise models and comparing what each one offered,” McClave said. “Bun Mee stood out because Denise and her team brought a level of professionalism and warmth that made the opportunity feel both promising and personal. The more we learned, the clearer it became that Bun Mee had the right mix of strong operations, a thoughtful leadership team, and the kind of offering that could thrive in New York City. Choosing Bun Mee was an easy decision after seeing how committed they are to doing things the right way.” The multi-unit development deal comes on the heels of Bun Mee’s 15th anniversary in April 2026, marking a milestone moment for the company. As the founding franchisees, the McClaves are helping usher Bun Mee into its next chapter, with plans to grow throughout the New York metro area. Their commitment sets the stage for a strong and promising franchise future. “The McClave family embodies everything Bun Mee was built on: their Vietnamese roots through Nam and Huy, their strong family bond, and the way they work together feels so familiar to my own story. Bun Mee is heavily rooted in food and family, so seeing those same values reflected in the McClaves makes this partnership incredibly special,” said Bun Mee founder and CEO Denise Tran. “Expanding into New York, one of the most competitive and food‑forward cities in the country, requires owners with heart and discipline. I believe the McClaves will set a strong foundation for the many franchise owners who will follow.” In 2025, Bun Mee saw national, regional and industry-wide recognition, with accolades from both Bloomberg and SFGATE recognizing Bun Mee’s San Francisco airport location as one of the top airport restaurants in the world. Additionally, Bun Mee was included again on Fast Casual’s Top 100 Movers and Shakers of 2025 , a testament to the industry’s recognition of the brand’s innovative footprint, authentic offerings and ambitious growth. Bun Mee’s franchise opportunity is powered by strong, fast‑growing unit economics. In 2025, it achieved an average unit volume (AUV) of $1,324,080.33 at traditional locations and $5,603,233.00 in non-traditional airport locations, reflecting rising demand for Vietnamese cuisine in an undersaturated category. Technology features like online ordering and contactless payment demonstrate Bun Mee’s modern fast‑casual positioning and focus on the customer experience, while sustainable ingredients and compostable packaging highlight its commitment to environmental responsibility. articles.title: KFC Celebrates Halloween Season with 13 Days of Promotions
articles.titleKo: KFC Celebrates Halloween Season with 13 Days of Promotions
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . KFC is celebrating Halloween with 13 consecutive days of limited-time promotions, offering a different deal each day from October 19 through October 31. The promotion, called “13 Days of Scary Good Deals,” includes discounted chicken sandwiches, tenders, wings, nuggets, and meals, along with free menu items with qualifying purchases. The daily offers include October 19: Free Classic Chicken Sandwich with a $5 purchase October 20: Free Wedges or Fries with a $5 purchase October 21: Two Snackers for $4 October 22: Free two-piece bone-in chicken with a $10 purchase October 23: 40 percent off a five-piece Tenders Combo October 24: $20 Chicken & Nugget Meal October 25: $15 eight-piece Tenders Meal October 26: Free Pot Pie with a purchase of $10 or more October 27: Free Famous Bowl with a $10 purchase October 28: 10 Wings for $10 October 29: Free Snacker with a $5 purchase October 30: 50 percent off a 12-piece chicken-only bucket October 31: 50 KFC Nuggets for $20 The promotion concludes on Halloween with the 50-piece nugget offer, which KFC is positioning as an option for families, parties, and other holiday gatherings. The 13-day promotion gives customers a different value offer each day leading up to Halloween. KFC did not specify participating locations, redemption channels, or additional promotional restrictions in the announcement.
